Hitman is a third-person stealth video game in which players take control of Agent 47, a genetically enhanced assassin, travelling to international locations and eliminating contracted targets. As in other games in the Hitman series, players are given a large amount of room for creativity in approaching their assassinations. For instance, players may utilize long-ranged rifles to snipe a target from a long distance, or they may decide to assassinate the target at close range by using blade weapons or garrote wire. Players can use explosives, or disguise the assassination by creating a seemingly accidental death. A common method to approach a mission is to incapacitate other characters and wear their outfits as a disguise, which allows the player to gain access to restricted areas more easily. Actions of non-playable characters influence the game. For instance, players can gain more information about the position of their target through listening to a nearby news reporter.
The level design of the game features a structure similar to that of Hitman: Blood Money and earlier games in the series, as opposed to the linear structure of Hitman: Absolution. Every episode in the game features a sandbox-type environment which can be explored by the player, featuring numerous ways to eliminate targets from accidents to scripted "opportunities" which require multiple tasks to complete. Levels are larger in Hitman, in which the maps in the game are "six to seven times larger than the biggest levels in Absolution". Levels accommodate about 300 non-playable characters (NPCs), with each having different routines and reacting differently to players' actions. Players can save their game anytime during missions. Instinct mode, which was introduced in Absolution, returns in a simplified form, no longer being an expendable resource. A player's mission performance review is rated on a 5-star rating system, influenced by factors such as time taken, number of non-targets killed, whether the player was spotted, whether or not they have been recorded on camera or if bodies were found. Completing challenges in a mission will award players with Mastery Points. Gaining enough mastery points will cause the player to earn a level of Mastery Level, with a total of 20 levels. As the player progresses through the 20 mastery levels, each level will earn players new items including new gadgets such as weapons, different types of poison and explosives, new agency pickup locations, or new starting locations.
IO Interactive introduced a "live component" to Hitman, with new content being delivered regularly in downloadable form. This includes time-limited missions called "Elusive Targets". If a player fails to assassinate an elusive target before the mission expires, or alert the target and allow them to escape, the target will not return. Successful completion of multiple targets yield cosmetic rewards for the player. "Escalation contracts", which are contracts created by the developers, include multiple stages that requires the player to complete certain tasks such as assassinating a target with a specific weapon or disguise or breaking into a safe. Completing a stage will progress through the escalation, and the difficulty will increase with new targets to assassinate, new challenges to comply with or new changes to the level. All additional downloadable content after release will be free of charge. Hitman: Absolution's online Contracts mode also returned in Hitman, allowing players to assign up to five NPCs as assassination targets, set requirements for how to kill them, and share their contract with other players to compete for high scores on.

Good game... but sadly not great. Only if developers could give it some more time and carefull planning.
So what is so good in it?
-Graphics are just so cool... models, enviroment... verything. Animations also nice. Well optimised.
-Mad max movies post apocalyptic feeling. It shows the world exactly as it was shown in movies. Just great... Ruins of human civilisation covered in dust where only strong and ruthless can have hope of survive. Every structure is build from rusted salvaged scrap. What remained of human population formed small communities fighting eachother for fuel water and food. No place for luxuries, health care, trust or friendship.
-Cars. Being tought as nails is not enough you need to be as mobile as posible. So you have your Opus Magnum piece of junk at the begining looking for a way to turn it into real monster killer. You will drive it a lot and fight in it a lot. Car fights are really cool. You need to be good driver and choose your tactics - use harpoon for pulling enemies vehicles, reaping their wheels of or just trying to impale their drivers. You can also target their fuel tanks with your shootgun or explosive spears. Or burn them with flamer...  Ram them or try to push them from the road... Sending them burning... how delightfull.
-Close combat. Simple but great. Multiple enemies with different fighting styles. Mostly trying to overwhelm you with greater numbers. You need to learn how to move to gain adventage when to block or avoid attacks. How to disarm or how to finish off enemies with your knife. You can punch... kick them, stab them with knife, shoot them at point blank range when they are closing. You can throw them, ram them kick them when they gone to the ground and much more. Violent and brutal.
-Large open world.
So why it is not great?
-Main story is well... rather poor.
-Side quests are very repetetive - clear minefields, destroy enemy convoy, take controll over enemy camps, loot for scrap. Those are fun but if you repeat it dozens of times it gets boring.
-No survival aspect. Water and fuel should be very limited and you should choose wisely when to use it and how. "Can I use this fuel cnister to set my enemies on fire or will I need it soon for my car?" But fuel is just everywhere. On every enemy camp you will find dozens of canisters and fuel tanks. And what are your mission objectives? Kill enemies inside camp and destroy fuel pump. Why not just take camp for you and secure fuel so you could use it to explore distant places? Just dumb... Same with ammo. If you upgrade Max so he could find and carry extra ammo you won`t be able to shoot everything but still you will have a lot of ammo and ways of resuplying it.
-Not much time on foot. Basically you will ride from one area to another then dismount and fight on food on location.
-Max customisation very poor. Actually there is just face customisation. Everything else is just upgraded.
-Close combat weapons... they are like made of glass... You can land courple of hits with them and they are gone. What is even more dumb... You cannot take them with you or even to your car.
-Max progression. I think you should be forced to choose if you want to be better at driving or fighting etc. Here you just get exp and become good in everything.
-Lack of stealth. You cannot sneak at all. It would be so great if you could decide if you want to kill your enemies in brutal melee or just sneak behind them and slit their throats or push them from the edge of cliff.
Some other things:
It should be roleplay... Really. Where you can interact with people, take some decissions about making alies and enemies. I don`t know it is about cash developers had on project but game simply lacking it.
I also don`t like idea of playing Max. I would love to make my own character in Mad Max world perhaps being able to meet him.
Well that is it. I give it 7.5/10.
Really worth a cash I spent on it. A lot of fun... but also a small degree of disapointment I feel looking at its potential that was wasted.

Overall I would suggest this game to anyone who enjoys this style of game. Sort of like Shadows of Mordor. It is very cheap now too for the amount of hours you will get out of it.

Spec Ops: The Line. There's one title I had never really noticed, until I came across it on a top something list of good games of some kind. It was lauded for its story.
The short version of this review is: everybody else is right, this is a recommendation, play it.
But why? Well, the game is a cover based, third person shooter. It gets the mechanics right except for one strange exception, being the melee button and the cover button being the same one. It's a reasonably small gripe, even if it caused a few deaths.
Graphically, the level design goes from OK-but-really-generic to very interesting and in service of the story and its progression. You'll have to get past the initial genericness of it, it's worth it. Technically, the game looks fine. It doesn't have anything revolutionairy going on, but that's not what Specs Ops is about.
You play as captain Walker, who, along with two team members is sent to Dubai on a reconnaissance mission. After finding something else than they expect, Walker decides that they're on a different mission now. But during this mission the line between what's right and what's wrong continues to shift and fade.
It's this story that's different from other games. Not the graphics, or the voice acting (which I think is very good btw), or the animations. Or rather: it's the idea that the game is more or less a character study, the type where at the end you think back and remember details that suddenly make sense. Or better yet: the details you missed that you notice the second time you play through it (these details are really a testament to the developer's devotion, massive thumbs up). It's is a pretty intense trip, and on the one hand it's about as much fun as it is to watch Apocalypse Now, but on the other hand, screw that and give this game a chance.

Been playing this game since mid September and played it recently when USA was released, to be honest i was really not on board with the episodic releases of each episode but im glad i waited until Bangkok was released to buy the full experience and play the levels that were available back to back. This game from the starting levels was great for me as it gave me a sense of de ja vu from Hitman: Blood Money with its minimal H.U.D and lack of hand holding.
The gameplay for this was in some way a hybrid of both Hitman: Blood Money and Hitman: Absolution with a lot less H.U.D than what Absolution had so the point system where they had your ranks displayed as well as point deductions and so on they are gone (Thank God) but there are slight pieces of information that displays that is not as in your face as Absolutions point system was so for example if you were to get rid of a civillian and take their clothes it would say "Non-Target Kill" and that is it no point deduction information no nothing, all of that information would be displayed when you finish the mission and it will give you a ranking as well as showing the point reductions themselves similar to Blood Money and Hitman games before.
When working on a level there are a number of ways to get into an area, take a disguise and walk past the guards, keep your starting clothes on and find a way in through alleyways, basements, kitchens etc, there are numbers of ways to go through this and now the targets themselves. Now getting the targets killed is in some way a challenge compared to absolution as in absolution you had to wait for an opportunity now in this game this does happen in areas where you might need to wait but in a good majority of the situations you would need to make the target go where you need to go so in some cases if you wear a disguise you can have the target follow you to a location where you can have the target be killed in a 'Accident' or if the target does not bring a bodyguard with them you can easily pop em with no trouble if you are quick enough to pull the gun aim and shoot because there is no slow mo s***e like what has  plagued some games in my opinon. the ways to eliminate a target are endless from what i can tell and feel as im playing the game, yes the intuition mode is back but it has been 'filtered' so to speak so there are now no player paths that are revealed but there are shadows that show NPC's and also show the main target in red similar to AC's Eagle Vison.
Contracts mode is back and is pratically the same as it was in Absolution but a good thing about this game is the new feature "Elsusive Targets" which gives players the chance to find new targets in the same maps such as Marrakesh, Bangkok, Paris etc. and eliminate them but its not as simple as that there are also outstanding rules and rewards when completing the contract but i will leave that for you to play if you want to buy this.
When it comes to the story this is a bit of a disappointment if your coming from absolution onto this because it does tip its hat to absolution but does not fully refer back to it in a way that would make this hitman a sequal. the cutscenes that are in the game are done very well with superb voice acting.
To give this a rating out of 10 it would be 7.9/10
Buy now whilst you have access to Elusive Targets
Note: there will be another review when the USA episode drops or maybe when the full experience is released on disc from what i have heard

I havn't been that much into FNAF games, the first one was good, the second one was ok, the third one was bad and the fourth one was ok. So I initially wasn't to excited for sister location since other horror games like Outlast 2 had my attention. However since it was on sale and because Outlast 2 was delayed, I decided to give this game a try. And to my suprise, Sister Location is a suprisingly good FNAF game, in fact probably the best in the series right now. There is now a full set of voice actors for the characters and they all do their job remarkably well. The game is also going for a noticably darker tone this time around with themes like torture and suicide coming into play. Despite the darker tone the game also a great sense of humor with the narrator occasionally cracking jokes that actually made me laugh and giving him a personality besides just telling what's going on. The jumpscares are a mixed bag, some of them are well animated and executed pretty decently and providing a very good sense of buildup that previous games struggled with (FNAF 3 especially). Some however don't have very good buildup and have pretty bland looking animations, this is exeptionally noticable in night 4 where the baby jumpscares just gets annoying (Foxy's isn't too good either). However the rest of the animatronic jumpscare are pretty good and I don't have any real issues with. The story is also very good in this game, I don't want to spoil any of it because it's just that good, just get the game and experience the story for yourself. Overall Sister Location is a very good improvment in both use of development time and cost as well as new directions for the series to go in, Sister Location is a good time for a very good majority of the time. I will give this game a 7.8/10

-Graphics are simple, yet very effective. There's a definite shine and polish to this one compared to the other games in the series with lots of moving parts, animations, and a great blend of dark atmosphere to set the mood properly. From a graphical and presentation standpoint, this is easily the best in the series.
-Sound design is top notch. Careful attention to detail was given to make sure the audio is what you focus on most while playing from listening to animatronics walking around the floors to the metallic groans of the facility. There is also full voice acting and a selection of different characters besides just one or two voices over the phone this time, each one matching their characters quite well.
-Story expands upon the universe in very subtle ways that aren't very noticable at first glance, and continue to flesh out the great lore of the series.
-Each night plays very different from the other, meaning the gameplay never gets stale as the nights go on.
-Difficulty curve is strangely high. The first 3 nights are fairly easy provided you take your time, but the fourth night proves a much harder challenge, while the 5th returns to being simple again
-Most of your enjoyment from the story in this will depend on if you've read Scott Cawthon's Five Nights at Freddy's book, The Silver Eyes. Those who haven't read it will not know who certain characters are and the ending will seem abrupt and convoluted.
-Much more narratively focused in terms of gameplay. While this is not necessarily a bad thing, it means that there's really no replay value save for finding secrets after completing the game, making it harder to recommend for its asking price. In line with this, there are no real cheats codes or unlockables that change the gameplay difficulty for added challenge (at least, none found yet. I will update this if the community does in fact find more then the 3 stars).
Another great entry into the series, provided you've done your homework beforehand, but with a lack of extra challenge modes or additional nights, it's harder to come back to and play again, unlike the previous entries. However, if you have a love for all things FNaF, this is an easy enough purchase to make.

-Leave It

It's good as a shooter, the vehicles are varied and fun to drive, and your customization options have no equal among any other game. You can literally use the in-game symbol editor to make a picture and then put that picture anywhere on your cars and clothing. It's also really intense on RAM so try to have 8GB as a minimum. Also, this game isn't compatible with multiple GPUs, so if you run more than one GPU then you'll have to turn off your Crossfire or whatever you use to link them. The shooting works for the most part but it's not really innovative. What sets the game apart is its open-world environment. You queue for and play missions, play some "cops 'n robbers" (criminals steal from open-world points and civilians, enforcers take their loot by witnessing them in the act and taking their ill-gotten gains), and explore and witness *other* players competing in their missions all in the same zone called a district. There's also districts for non-stop team deathmatch and objective play without queueing.
The community and game performance on most machines would be the weakest points I can talk about. Something about this game doesn't run on most computers without freezeframing every so often, especially when you're trying to approach a corner to use for cover without overshooting it and getting shot to death out in the open. "Screenshot time" happens to me frequently and it's just plain frustrating. Many players that chat a lot tend to be about as smart as a sack of hammers. They rant accusations of cheating at any who best them and can't spell or put together an intelligible sentence.
It's free to play so give it a shot. The shooting will take some getting used to and you might have to put up with fighting against players who have guns and mods that synergise to produce a just plain better weapon that new players need to earn through some amount of playing.

If you like open world games that are similar to Far Cry in some ways (enemy camps to take down, upgrading your character and armament...) and love the Mad Max universe you should definitely consider getting this game.
The big selling point of this game is its atmosphere which is really really well done and really puts you right in the midst of the Mad Max dystopian world.
Contrary to what one might think there is a lot of things to discover in the Wasteland and it's a real joy to be able to roam freely in it.
Of course, being a Mad Max game, the devs put a lot of work on the vehicles and they really nailed it, there is a lot to improve on your own car but you can also collect enemy cars and use them as cover or for their unique weaponry.
In the end I was really impressed by this game that I picked up for around $5 without a lot of expectations being a game inspired by a movie but was really pleasantly surprised by the depth and the attention to detail the devs put into it.
Now I just have to aim for the 100% completion or I might just never stop playing!

Good game... but sadly not great. Only if developers could give it some more time and carefull planning.
So what is so good in it?
-Graphics are just so cool... models, enviroment... verything. Animations also nice. Well optimised.
-Mad max movies post apocalyptic feeling. It shows the world exactly as it was shown in movies. Just great... Ruins of human civilisation covered in dust where only strong and ruthless can have hope of survive. Every structure is build from rusted salvaged scrap. What remained of human population formed small communities fighting eachother for fuel water and food. No place for luxuries, health care, trust or friendship.
-Cars. Being tought as nails is not enough you need to be as mobile as posible. So you have your Opus Magnum piece of junk at the begining looking for a way to turn it into real monster killer. You will drive it a lot and fight in it a lot. Car fights are really cool. You need to be good driver and choose your tactics - use harpoon for pulling enemies vehicles, reaping their wheels of or just trying to impale their drivers. You can also target their fuel tanks with your shootgun or explosive spears. Or burn them with flamer...  Ram them or try to push them from the road... Sending them burning... how delightfull.
-Close combat. Simple but great. Multiple enemies with different fighting styles. Mostly trying to overwhelm you with greater numbers. You need to learn how to move to gain adventage when to block or avoid attacks. How to disarm or how to finish off enemies with your knife. You can punch... kick them, stab them with knife, shoot them at point blank range when they are closing. You can throw them, ram them kick them when they gone to the ground and much more. Violent and brutal.
-Large open world.
So why it is not great?
-Main story is well... rather poor.
-Side quests are very repetetive - clear minefields, destroy enemy convoy, take controll over enemy camps, loot for scrap. Those are fun but if you repeat it dozens of times it gets boring.
-No survival aspect. Water and fuel should be very limited and you should choose wisely when to use it and how. "Can I use this fuel cnister to set my enemies on fire or will I need it soon for my car?" But fuel is just everywhere. On every enemy camp you will find dozens of canisters and fuel tanks. And what are your mission objectives? Kill enemies inside camp and destroy fuel pump. Why not just take camp for you and secure fuel so you could use it to explore distant places? Just dumb... Same with ammo. If you upgrade Max so he could find and carry extra ammo you won`t be able to shoot everything but still you will have a lot of ammo and ways of resuplying it.
-Not much time on foot. Basically you will ride from one area to another then dismount and fight on food on location.
-Max customisation very poor. Actually there is just face customisation. Everything else is just upgraded.
-Close combat weapons... they are like made of glass... You can land courple of hits with them and they are gone. What is even more dumb... You cannot take them with you or even to your car.
-Max progression. I think you should be forced to choose if you want to be better at driving or fighting etc. Here you just get exp and become good in everything.
-Lack of stealth. You cannot sneak at all. It would be so great if you could decide if you want to kill your enemies in brutal melee or just sneak behind them and slit their throats or push them from the edge of cliff.
Some other things:
It should be roleplay... Really. Where you can interact with people, take some decissions about making alies and enemies. I don`t know it is about cash developers had on project but game simply lacking it.
I also don`t like idea of playing Max. I would love to make my own character in Mad Max world perhaps being able to meet him.
Well that is it. I give it 7.5/10.
Really worth a cash I spent on it. A lot of fun... but also a small degree of disapointment I feel looking at its potential that was wasted.

Picked this up for $4.22 US. The car combat in this game is a breath of fresh air for games in this Genre. Where you have some time between points of interest to just enjoy the views and hammer the nitrous! One of my favorite things in this game is when you are doing whatever and you get that STORM WARNING! I love how you can see it far off in the distance then try to outrun it and BOOM you are in the thick of it! With a solid sound system the engines, storms and other effects sound great. That feel you get from Harpooning a door of and then pulling the driver out with it is also fantastic and never gets old. I started pulling guys out of the front window, haha!
If I had to make any negative comments, well there would be some things. Firstly you get the V8 Unlocks a bit late in the storyline as myself I am a completionist and before pushing the story too far I cleared all the optional things but looking back I would do the storyline first then the optional stuff. I ran into a few glitches too. Once I got out of my vehicle and it still registered me having my harpoon equipped instead of my shotgun. I also took a long drink of water one time and had the water splashing on face animation continue on my hand till I loaded into a stronghold. There were a few spots where I did manage to get stuck and had to fast travel to a Stronghold.
Overall I would suggest this game to anyone who enjoys this style of game. Sort of like Shadows of Mordor. It is very cheap now too for the amount of hours you will get out of it.

This game is simply amazing to be honest. My friends laugh at me because I drive trucks for hours and yes, that's what you do, but that's the addictive part actually. Why is it addictive?
- Because you start with basically nothing, you'll have to start as a small employee and do a few jobs to earn enough money and buy your first truck. You can also take a loan but I prefer saving up on my own.. I hate getting f*cked by the interest rate Xd and it simply feels better to work hard for what you want.
- Once you have your truck you can do whatever you want, (mainly jobs but you can roam arround if you wish). Through your career you will earn XP and level up and obviously, you'll unlock new trucks and new parts that you can add to those trucks (Better engines, better transmissions, new chassis, new cabins, new interiors, new paintjobs,better tires and so on...)
- Afterwards, once you get enough money, you can buy another truck and hire a driver that will work for your company, you will get money everyday and the longer he works, the more he'll give to you and you'll be able to expand your company and hire more drivers.
The other amazing thing is this game's modding community, it has one of the best map mods (ProMods ; TSM ; RusMap and so on... they add countries/islands/cities that SCS hasn't worked on yet and add their own scenery but they are very close to reality, even better than SCS' vanilla sceneries. Note that the latest DLCs SCS are releasing are as amazing); People make mods for almost anything from gauges to super engine mods, it's simply amazing how huge the modding community is and that's what keeps the game going in my opinion. There's even a multiplayer mod if you wish to play with your friends, it's full of people and usually very busy but if you like it why not? No wonder why this game is so well rated, it got out in 2012 and still rocks and that's because of this amazing dev. team and the huge community behind it (I got the boxed edition back then and still play it since 2012 lol)
Okay, now everything is amazing yeah but there are a few cons. This game is stable, you can run it on very low end PCs and on high end ones as well. That's not an issue, the issue is that you can get very bad fps drops in cities because of the "meh" graphical engine they are using. (With mods especially, otherwise, I wouldn't bother). The graphics are amazing for a 2012 game, it's a good engine but it's starting to get very old and unoptimized for huge map mods for example, 30FPS in some cities with a 970 and an OC'd 6600K. The vanilla game runs alright for me but I also get a few drops in big cities. Note that it's a simulator, 30 FPS is very playble just not pleasant to the eye from time to time.
TL;DR : ETS2 is a very relaxing and addictive game, you will have to grind to get your company going and make some moolah,heh. The modding community is HUGE! There are mods for almost anything and the game is always getting updated since 2012 and it still ROCKS. The graphics are amazing for a 2012 game but it has one con which is the old graphical engine, the fps drops can affect you sometimes in huge cities but it's very playable even if you get drops, it's a simulator.
You still hesitate? Ask a friend if he has it and try it in familiy view, you can watch gameplays but I usually don't like watching someone play ETS2... it is very boring. So... if you like relaxing games, ETS2 is a good choice, I'd say it's one of the best games out there "chill-wise". It's a drug :D

“The truth, Walker, is that you're here because you wanted to feel like something you're not: A hero.” Without wishing to spoil anything, these words were spoken in the recent game Spec-Ops: The Line. One question that often comes up with video games is what advantage a game has over a movie or a book? The answer to that is the level of interaction that a person has with a game’s world and story. I’ve read movies and books that can get a person to think about the actions that a person may take, but I have never seen or read anything that makes me question my own actions. This is where the game Spec Ops: The Line comes in, and it really does do a great job at responding to the actions of the player with actual consequences unlike other games. While the gameplay is very standard the story telling is probably some of the best stories told in video games in recent time.
A recent problem with the game industry is the slew of modern shooters paving the way for very uncomfortable themes. For example Call of Duty: Ghosts’ story is about America building a doomsday cannon in space- and the game has no self-awareness whatsoever. The game doesn’t get much better when the player gains control of the cannon and nukes all of South America. So the theme to Call of Duty: Ghosts comes across as being that America should build a death weapon to kill everyone who isn’t American. Thank goodness for Spec-Ops: The Line coming along and showing us how a deep and complex story should be told. While the gameplay is certainly standard in this game, it goes along with telling the absolutely excellent story. It’s one of the few games that everyone should play. Whether one plays games or not, it’s a game that gets people to think with its innovative story telling.
Spec Ops: The Line is based on the book Heart of Darkness by Joseph Conrad, which was also the inspiration for the movie Apocalypse Now. The basic plotline of those pieces is that a Colonel in the army goes native deep in the heart of jungle lands and starts ruling over the native population. That’s not a spoiler, for those who are wondering. It is established very early on in Spec Ops: The Line that Col. John Konrad (the main antagonist) is ruling over the native populace. The game also doesn’t borrow that much from Apocalypse Now or Heart of Darkness. The reason that the Colonel has decided to ditch the US army and go native is that a recent sandstorm has struck the Middle Eastern city of Dubai. After the major politicians and other VIPs leave the city Konrad is ordered to abandon the city and come home to America. Konrad chooses to stay in the city along with his unit, the 33rd infantry, which would become known as the “Damned 33rd.” The colonel and his troops made one last desperate escape attempt, but failed miserably. The city went dark for six months before American forces received a radio message from Konrad asking for aid.
Enter our protagonists, Captain Martin Walker and his two NPC (non-player character) subordinates. The first thoughts that I had going into this was that it was going to be another Call of Duty clone. I was expecting another gun ho, nationalistic war game about how great it is to go to war. However, the game pulls a massive fast one though when, in the context of war, the game has the player do something unforgivable. I know that I felt like crap after it happened. After this event, Walker’s mind begins a massive descent into madness and brutality as he moves toward a goal that is becoming increasingly blurred. What I like about the game’s story is how it starts. The player starts with the expectations they would have about any modern game, which makes the grand twist all the more shocking. Those who tend to look at modern shooters with disdain would especially find the moment to be a huge shock to them when they find themselves questioning their own morality.
However, some people though may find the tone to be a bit wonky at times, especially in regards to the gameplay. One bullet from your gun is enough blow an entire enemy’s head clean off, with bone sticking out of the neck stump. It also does that thing where it slows down the gameplay so you can get a good look at your freshly slain kill. These features do seem to go against the actual message of the game, but I feel as though this was intended to let the player lose his or her self in the game before the game yanks on the collar and pulls the player back down to reality. On the other hand, however, it’s almost like if someone flashes you in the parking lot and then yells at you for looking. I never asked to see those violent kills in Spec Ops, so I wouldn’t be surprised if a few people were turned off because of this. Keep in mind, though, I could have stopped playing at any time, so that’s what makes me believe that the game was making me lose myself in the first half and then begin the spiral into madness. One of the more important questions, though, is “how does the gameplay work?”
The gameplay itself is a basic third person cover based shooter with tactical elements. I think that the third person really goes along with creating a sense of disconnect between the player and the character. This makes it so it doesn’t feel like the player is just being lectured by the game and goes to show the effects these actions can have on a soldier. If it had been in the first person a lot of what it was trying to say would have been lost. No one likes to be told how to feel. In Amnesia: The Dark Descent the game had a sanity meter which would tell you how scared you should be, which seems to say that the developers were not very confident with their own work. While the final confrontation is as much confronting the player as it is Walker, if it had been done from the first person perspective it would have felt more like a lecture at the player forcing them to feel bad. As for the tactical part the game, it’s probably the weaker aspect. You point at a group of soldiers you particularly don’t like, and your explosives guy will blow it up. You point at a faraway enemy you don’t like and your sniper guy will shoot it. These effects don’t go toward much and are barely used because it’s does not take long before you realize that it is easier to eliminate the middle man and just shoot them yourself. The tactical part of the game falls flat so what else is there?
A unique selling point to the game is its use of sand. Sometimes you can shoot out windows to have a huge ton of sand come crashing down on top the enemies, but it’s hardly worth mentioning. It’s not going to make any one jump up and down. What I found most interesting about the gameplay was the development of the character shown through his actions. You can perform executions with your enemy. At first it start as a way to end someone’s life painlessly, but as Walker’s mind collapses he starts wanting to cause as much pain to his enemies as possible. This is also shown in his dialogue during combat. At the start he would shout “he’s down” and by the end of it he would shout “F***ing stay dead!” I do like how well the gameplay goes to show Walker’s descent into madness. One other thing that I love is the focus it keep as the game progresses.
I have heard some complaints about how the game is too linear, but I don’t buy that. If you are going for a very story and character centered game then you should go with linearity. This keeps the game focused and on task. In a game like Grand Theft Auto IV, which had a fantastic main character, a lot of the drama was lost in the sandbox. There could be a scene that could put The Godfather to shame but once you were out in the sandbox and was able pile up the bodies of ten people and do a ramp off of them in a flaming car into the river, all sense of drama would be lost. A game like Spec Ops: The Line needed to be linear to keep the focus on Walker and his own journey.

This game gives back equal to what it gets from the player. If you step in for an hour or two you won't get very far, probably left thinking it is a lame game with a very foreign comic-esc artstyle. This RPG-FPS hybrid is a dreamworld for the curious, a playground for the sharp of wit, a pattern interrupt for the FPS community.
Modern (and old) FPS games do a decent job of crafting worlds where the mantra of "Kill Or Be Killed" does not become too boring. The campaigns are typically very directed, but for the most part the game kills a deviating player. I still like FPS games. Specifically I love the Halo franchise even if I have qualms with the direction 343 wants to go; but that is for a different review. FPS's are fantastic and the Borderlands franchise draws upon the strengths from that field of gaming. It is just that Borderlands 2 is not solely a FPS that draws you into its story within the first hours of playing. It is a slow build where the journey is part of the reward.
Borderlands 2 is a RPG as well as a FPS. RPG's revel in custom playstyles and BL2 is no exception. It has six characters, each with three skill trees, and only 68 skill points and it takes around 42 to fill a skill tree. There is a lot of room allowing players to develop their character as they desire especially in the weapons they choose to use. Combining everything with the freedom, even encouragement, to deviate from the main storyline Borderlands 2 upholds the nature of RPG's at the same time. FPS fast paced violence combined with RPG customization, imho, fosters innate curiosity. This playground for the curious serves as a pattern interrupt for the FPS gamer and a comic relief for the RPG gamer.
Sadly this is a very DLC based game, but the GOTY edition is a perfect summation of the essentials of BL2. From there Ultimate Upgrade 2 is the frosting on the cake and the rest can be sprinkled in as you desire. Recommendations for a prospective Vault Hunter? Wait till a sale, good ones are Black Friday, Christmas, or Summer Sales, then get the GOTY edition, commit to play the complete storyline as a minimum and then pick your on sale DLC’s as you choose. Happy Hunting!

Shiver: Vanishing Hitchhiker is the first in a series of beautifully crafted, horror-themed hidden object titles by Artogon Games.  Originally released in 2011, the game holds up incredibly well even by today’s standards.  An excellent example of a hidden object and adventure game hybrid (HOPA), it appeals to both HOG and Adventure gamers alike.  With a chilling story that lacks  the campiness of other games, somewhat challenging point ‘n’ click gameplay, and breathtakingly gorgeous artwork, there’s very little for me to complain about when it comes to this classic of the hidden object genre.
Everything about Vanishing Hitchhiker screams quality, from the realistically painted landscapes and beautifully decaying building interiors to the atmospherically creepy sound design and soundtrack, a lot of love went into this game.  Even the few lines of spoken narration are acted without the over the top melodrama we so often get in the genre.  That’s to say nothing of the story, which is an interesting take on ghostly hitchhiker tales, and it refreshingly goes in an unexpected direction to boot. I truly wish the game were longer, as 6 hours in Gordon Creek wasn’t nearly long enough for this lover of creepy horror stories.

Although gameplay is your standard HOPA fare, I felt the challenge of the adventure elements was slightly higher than I’m used to in these titles, at least on Advanced mode.  While the plentiful hidden object scenes are helpfully denoted with sparkles, there were many a time I found myself wandering without a clue as to how to proceed, and had embarrassingly resorted to the HINT button more times than I’m willing to admit.  However, the game nudges you along if you’re stumped for too long and will sparkle on areas of interest if you’ve been sitting without progress for an extended period of time.  Normally, I’d be annoyed with this unrequested help, especially on Advanced mode, but I found it more than welcome here as the intricately detailed images sometimes make it difficult to figure out where to focus on next.
Outside of the lack of achievements, which is something I always champion for here on Steam, my sole complaint is with the low resolution of the game screen.  Of course, this was released before wide screen was the industry standard, and most casual gamers were playing on older monitors and systems. Unfortunately, that means you either play in a smaller Windowed Mode which maintains the beauty of the original graphical resolution, or stretched out in Widescreen Mode.  Thankfully, there’s a Widescreen Correction option that un-stretches the image, but it places black bars on either side of the screen.  Although I personally find that preferable to playing with the gorgeous artwork stretched out, fuzzy, and distorted, you’re not going to get an unaltered 1920 x 1080 image from the game, which may be unacceptable for some players.
If you’re looking for a good, creepy, hidden object adventure with a story that’s unsettling without being over-the-top cheesy, Vanishing Hitchhiker is your game.  Despite playing it years ago over at Big Fish, I loved it just as much (if not more) my second time through, and I know without a doubt I’ll be visiting Gordon Creek again and again.  Now, if only the other games in the Shiver series make it over to Steam, my life may well be complete.
Bottom Line: Highly Recommended to both hidden object and adventure gamers.

It was pure luck that I recognized this game as being one probably published by Big Fish Games. Indeed, I've come back to Neoseeker and I am currently adding many casual adventures/HO games. The series Shiver was one of these planned to be added soon. By releasing the game here, BFG prompted me to quicken the process.
However, I couldn't resist the purchase, as it was close to the kind of ambiance I prefer for this kind of game. So, in the end, was it really worth of my wallet?
You took a hitchhiker with you and let her go at Gordon Creek. However, the teddy bear she forgets looked like one in your childhood and decided to give it back to the mysterious girl. But did you really expect to find her easily in that gloomy and deserted town?
The plot was beginning well: a mysterious sad woman, a teddy bear, a gloomy town, anything that can be tied to a psychological game, with people being used for experiments... My imagination was running so wild that in the end, the story seemed to be a little disappointing. I still don't understand why the little boy leads you to finish your quest, when you're clearly on your way to find the truth. And the extra chapter should have been included in the main story. It would have been more logical for the plot.
Anyway, the gameplay is the same as any other game of the kind: you find items, you use them, you solve puzzles, though they're rare, you clear hidden objects scenes. The novelty here is the fact that you're carrying a flashlight and a camera with you, used to lit darker areas and to take pictures. You can take them anytime but there are moments where you need to do that to go forward. Generally, it will blink to show you that you need the picture of a vision or a ghost.
If I have a regret, it's probably for the hidden objects scenes: some objects aren't really visible and given the dark nature of the game, it's not really helping.
The graphics are really good for the ambiance, though I would have probably liked a more developed burial site. It would have strengthened the supernatural side than what happened in the town or on the island.
The soundtrack is really nice too and very fitting. However, the voice acting could have been better: I didn't feel like the man had really emotions.
As a collector's edition, you'll find the bonus chapter, concept arts, etc.. Nothing really extraordinary, as some other games are more furnished for that domain.
Anyway, Shiver: Vanishing Hitchhiker disappointed me because I was expecting something else but is a good moment to pass. However, I find the price a little too high for what it is really.  I do hope that Big Fish Games will finally understand that participating in sales on Steam can be a good idea, like they did with Mystery Cases Files, where I ended up buying those discounted. Because if they're discounting other games like Awakening, Dark Tales, Otherworld or even Dark Parables, I would acquire them without problems.

Been playing this game since mid September and played it recently when USA was released, to be honest i was really not on board with the episodic releases of each episode but im glad i waited until Bangkok was released to buy the full experience and play the levels that were available back to back. This game from the starting levels was great for me as it gave me a sense of de ja vu from Hitman: Blood Money with its minimal H.U.D and lack of hand holding.
The gameplay for this was in some way a hybrid of both Hitman: Blood Money and Hitman: Absolution with a lot less H.U.D than what Absolution had so the point system where they had your ranks displayed as well as point deductions and so on they are gone (Thank God) but there are slight pieces of information that displays that is not as in your face as Absolutions point system was so for example if you were to get rid of a civillian and take their clothes it would say "Non-Target Kill" and that is it no point deduction information no nothing, all of that information would be displayed when you finish the mission and it will give you a ranking as well as showing the point reductions themselves similar to Blood Money and Hitman games before.
When working on a level there are a number of ways to get into an area, take a disguise and walk past the guards, keep your starting clothes on and find a way in through alleyways, basements, kitchens etc, there are numbers of ways to go through this and now the targets themselves. Now getting the targets killed is in some way a challenge compared to absolution as in absolution you had to wait for an opportunity now in this game this does happen in areas where you might need to wait but in a good majority of the situations you would need to make the target go where you need to go so in some cases if you wear a disguise you can have the target follow you to a location where you can have the target be killed in a 'Accident' or if the target does not bring a bodyguard with them you can easily pop em with no trouble if you are quick enough to pull the gun aim and shoot because there is no slow mo s***e like what has  plagued some games in my opinon. the ways to eliminate a target are endless from what i can tell and feel as im playing the game, yes the intuition mode is back but it has been 'filtered' so to speak so there are now no player paths that are revealed but there are shadows that show NPC's and also show the main target in red similar to AC's Eagle Vison.
Contracts mode is back and is pratically the same as it was in Absolution but a good thing about this game is the new feature "Elsusive Targets" which gives players the chance to find new targets in the same maps such as Marrakesh, Bangkok, Paris etc. and eliminate them but its not as simple as that there are also outstanding rules and rewards when completing the contract but i will leave that for you to play if you want to buy this.
When it comes to the story this is a bit of a disappointment if your coming from absolution onto this because it does tip its hat to absolution but does not fully refer back to it in a way that would make this hitman a sequal. the cutscenes that are in the game are done very well with superb voice acting.
To give this a rating out of 10 it would be 7.9/10
Buy now whilst you have access to Elusive Targets
Note: there will be another review when the USA episode drops or maybe when the full experience is released on disc from what i have heard

Optimalization is also great, I was pretty concerned with my notebook with low frequency i7 and GF 650M but it runs smoothly. I can do full hd with basically anything  which influence how the models etc look on high without a problem. I could probably afford to set some stuff a bit higher but it looks great anyway so there is really no need.
Control settings also has a good quality for console ports. I didnt have a problem to bind any buttons I needed. Very often the games cant differentiate between regular enter and numerical one and dont recognize few keys but I had no problem here.
What I probably like the most about this game is that speacial allure of sorts where although I dont really need to do all that small insignificant stuff and collect all that (s)crap I still enjoy doing it in every new location for some reason even though it is in its essense just a boring repetitive work.
There are basically only 3 things which I dont really "like".
First, I would like to see a possibility to use sniper rifle even outside of vehicle.
Second, the low amount of human models. Almost all quest/informatuon givers look the same and same can be said about "bosses". They also look alike and the only difference is the color of warpaint.
Third, not possible to fast travel and keep different vehicle outside of basic one. Kind of pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to clear minefieds if you have to drive all that distance :D
Anyway 9,5/10 for me and definitely worth buying even at full prize but grab it in sale if you can like with any game even the best ones :D

Let me just start by saying I love APB, but it is victim to many flaws. APB is worth a try for anyone into competitive shooters, combined with an open world, GTA feeling in the background. This game is fun but it has quite a few huge problems.
- Sometimes matchmaking will be un-even and making teams just terribly balanced. Which will make you mad and what not.
- P2W does have an aspect here. Most guns are just re-skins of the F2P weapons but P2W weapons come with amazing modifications that to low-mid tier players, makes the guns feel extremely over-powered. Really when buying a weapon you're paying for awesome mods, in most cases.
- Hackers can be a huge nusance. I have only ran into a fair share of blatant hackers who do it just to make people mad. Although I have not played since FairFight was introduced and I heard it has been doing quite well. Along with FairFight in Battlefield 4 which took a lot of hackers out. So hackers can be a problem but it is nice seeing the devs get something fresh for the fight against hacks.
- Performance can be an issue for a lot of people. I have quite a beastly rig so I do just fine but my friends PC's aren't necessarily as powerful and they can get that bad stutter from the HDD trying to fetch all the items and what not from the server/client. So not really a problem for me but I know for some it can be a fun killer.
With all of that said. Those for me are the bigger issues that will leave people frustrated and angry over APB. Let me tell you though. When you get into a balanced game, with good players all around, there is a silver lighting. When the game is being played how it should be, it is truly something special. That is why I love APB. When it is done right, you will find the love and perfection of the game. It is a fun, competitive shooter that will give you that ♥♥♥♥ yeah, this is awesome feeling. Once APB gives you that, it will get you quite hooked. Especially when you play with friends. The problem is it isn't like that all the time.
All in all, I do recommend this game because it can be so fun, but take caution and note this game comes with it's fair share of frustration.

If a game does not have me hooked by the first 4 hours of gameplay, I immediately set it aside and give it a negative review.
Call it unfair, not giving the game a chance: I did....I really wanted to like this game.
In fact, the concepts and execution of the game are not what I have problems with: it's the fanbase.
Literally the most ANNOYING thing I hear constantly comes from the fanbase. That's not to bash those who enjoy this game...but there are those who take things a bit far. That's what I hate to see come from a videogame with such promise, only to be crushed by its obnoxious fanbase.
Now, it's 2017, and this came out in late 2015, so 2 years since it came out, and maybe the fanbase has died out a little, but by GOD at the time, all I kept getting bashed for was not giving the game a chance.
Let me tell you something about the gameplay: it's interesting, it's refreshing, but goddamn it is the most BROKEN AF system I have seen. Literally combat and evading damage is not used through stats or chance %s, it's all your ability to dodge and control a huge heart piece in the middle of D-Day on Normandy Beach....that is the equivalent to trying not to take damage.
Now granted, I could have taken time to hone this, but why bother? I could be playing way more entertaining, more intuitive games. And of course, this doesn't mean I wasn't up to the challenge, but I think the reason it didn't work for me was the payoff and reward factor was so empty and non-existent that I didn't even feel motivated to complete a boss.
Of course, the humor and story are FLAWLESS, and the fact you can choose to be a proned pacifist or a determined fighter is really intriguing (if you know what you're doing).
All in all, I DO think people should give this game a try, but be warned: the game is more fun to watch than it is to play.
Also, f*ck Sans......and I know why, don't question my logic....

This game is good. It's good because it states an idea. An idea that shows a perspective. A perspective that gives a realization. A realization that blows the mind. Not many games can make you sit there just wondering: " Why did I do that?, What was I thinking?, What is wrong with me?" This game does that. It's gameplay being similar with COD's gameplay: shoot and kill anyone who appears to be an enemy. Yet the whole game itself is so different, so unique, so beautiful. Spec. Ops: The Line may not look like much at first glance, but it presents an experience that would blow a person's mind. It changes a person's perspective on several things: war, death, life, etc.. It's graphics may not be much but that won't matter compared to the beauty of the game's story. It's soundtrack is pretty decent but nothing spectacular. It's characters molded so carefully and so beautifully. In summary, I'd like to say that this game is a experience recommended for all gamers who typically enjoy FPS games. Not that it isn't for other gamers but it would work especially well on these specific gamers.
(P.S.: Please do search up a story explanation after game completion if you feel that you have any confusions or misconceptions with the game.)

A fairly mediocre experience to me as it really was just trying to tell a story deeper than the gameplay. The story itself presents itself as serious, and the voice acting helps it but the gameplay does not. One moment it'll be tense and strong while it cuts to the next section of gameplay and you're back to hardened war veterans. Much like Lara Croft in Tomb Raider, this game has the characters changing in cutscenes, but once the game gives you back control, you're back on headshot island starring Nathan Drake.
Everyone found this story to be compelling, and I sadly found it to be lackluster since the gameplay ruined the pacing. You have serious conversations with pop quiz moment decisions yet the gameplay doesn't reflect that as you're killing NPCs left and right without consequence. I even accidentally killed a civilian and the game chugged along like nothing happened. It was literally wave after wave of enemies, then to the next checkpoint before we start another wave of enemies. It got pretty boring well into Chapter 5/13, which I reached within only an hour of gameplay. I wished that this game had more heart than it does soul. I really couldn't grip myself into the story because I saw it and played it like any other Call of Duty. This isn't The Last of Us, or even Uncharted with tight controls, great voice acting and impeccable storytelling. I feel like it's closer to Tomb Raider, with it's decent controls and average story. +1 for being original and having a good setting, but to me; that wasn't enough to save this game. Sorry.

Of course, this was solely my experience and it seemed like the other 90k people felt the exact opposite, so check this game out if you want to try something different, but not too different that it doesn't feel familiar to the likes of Army of Two or Gears of War. 5/10.

I'm a huge fan of Hitman going back to the original game on my first PC after many many old Mac computers.  My brother and I played the original and the sequel so many times it's bordering on sickness. We are big fans of Contracts as well and Blood Money is the refinement of the series entire philosophy. You don't really need more Hitman games after that point-which Absolution deftly proved. You can't or you shouldn't mess with perfection-even though the game is eye candy for fans of the original series, the narrative was pedestrian at best, and at worst an unwatchable mess. No one plays the Hitman games for the story, really- his origin is a joke and those levels only work as an intro to the playstyle-his actual origin story is incredibly weak.
The new game respects the amount of narrative that was found in the original and somewhat meets it in the middle of Absolution, without the vapid trashy vibe of that game.  I love how open the levels are and they remind me of the best levels in Blood Money and Absolution, and thankfully with the episodic nature, you're given ample time to best through each level without powering through a whole narrative. I appreciate it. I've never been one to play through any game all at once, and with Hitman especially-eveyone has their favorite levels they return to...this is just a simplified version of what the real hardcore fans of the franchise wanted.  Sure, is it mildly annoying to wait a month between installments? Yes, a little bit-but you should be aware of what you're paying for before you put your hard earned money down. I like the casual vibe of being able to, and encouraged to explore as much as possible-the exact opposite of Absolution.  I do wish they'd just make another game like Blood Money- a full single player, wide open and epic experience, but perhaps that model of game is no longer en vogue for all but the most prestige AAA titles.  I believe something more like Grand Theft Auto or Red Dead Redemption would suit this series best, a fully realized full explorable world, not limited to a city, where you can hop on a plane and travel the globe, explore without missions and canvas buildings before your hits to plan things out, but for now this game will do, and it does it marvelously.

I guess I will recommend the game based upon the interesting environment, idea of storytelling and endings. However it has some major issues with the controls..being god awful. You'll find yourself frequently frustrated when you die, not due to your own error, but the game's faulty controls.
Some examples: You cannot go in cover, if you are out of cover reloading. At certain points, shooting someone will result in the camera shaking and going in slow-motion making it harder to hit with certain weapons. So many actions is linked to the same button... you will find yourself using shift to both bash enemies and jump barriers. Space-bar is heal, cover, run and actions. R is both reload, loot ammo and pick up weapon.
Weapons on the soldiers you kill will sometimes not drop their weapon, so you risk running out of ammo (mostly an early game problem). As you can only carry two weapons no matter the type, you cannot carry say a pistol and two larger guns. Which given the main guy's very clear pistol holster is rather puzzling.
There is clearly holes in the plot, and story elements visible way of, but you might also find yourself being surprised.
All in all I will recommend it, just keep the problems in mind.

This isn't just a game, it's existential art.  This should be required playing for every high school student in America.  It forces you to question your own ideas on what constitutes a hero, what an enemy is, what the nature of duty is, what is good, what is bad, what is right, what is wrong, what is honorable, what is dishonorable, what is justice, what is moral, and who gets to decide where to draw the line.
The story pivots around the central character's hero complex and his need to validate this egoistic image he has of himself.  He makes bad decisions and commits to them even when the outcome of those decisions leads to disastrous consequences.  He never takes responsibility for his poor choices, because his ego won't allow him to, but instead insists that he "had no choice".  By the end of the game the player, too, will feel his/her expectations challenged.  This metagaming experience will leave a lasting impression.
This game has a pretty thick narrative that mostly plays out in dialogue between the various actors as they move through the world.  Cutscenes are concise and to the point.  There is no filler here.   This is very much a modern day retelling of the Joseph Conrad novel 'Heart of Darkness'.  The story had me hooked from beginning to end.  The writing is that good!
Gameplay-wise it functions like many third person shooter games (Gears of War, for instance).  Some of the mechanics can be wonky, but not to the detriment of "enjoyment".  You can carry two weapons at a time and 3 different explosive types (grenade, sticky bomb, and flashbang).  You can swap for weapons you come across, and you can find ammo and explosive boxes to refill what you're carrying.  There is a plethora of weapons and they all have their pros and cons.  There are also places where you can man turrets or gatling guns.
Combat involves alot of taking cover and picking your shots.  Doom this is not.  It's very easy to get torn to shreds by a hail of bullets in seconds if you're not careful.  There are no medkits, your health regenerates when not taking damage, but your team-mates can be incapicated - injecting them with morphine helps get them back into action (if they bleed out first they die and you restart at a checkpoint).
The graphics are gorgeous.  The game has beautiful scenery with a rich tapestry of colors that belies the dark nature of the world you inhabit.  It has it's share of gore, but it's a story about war which is always messy.
The voiceover acting is impeccable.  The sound design is solid.  The soundtrack is amazing.
Multiplayer is a mixed bag, but if you have no interest in the singleplayer game and it's metaphysical storytelling then you should probably go play Battlefield or some other brainless shooter instead anyway.

Borderlands 2 is an immeasurably fun experience, from the four different classes to the varying, beautiful landscapes, it certainly brings the world of Pandora to life. The humour of the game is perfectly interwoven into the story and gameplay, as it is used rather subtly and appropriately, as if actual people were making the jokes and not characters from a sitcom. Ridiculous characters make ridiculous entrances, and serious moments are reacted to appropriately by all.
"Man, this is one of them moments..... CATCH A RIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIDE!"
The game has a massive variety of enemies throughout the world that contribute to the believability of Pandora, as each area has creatures to fit the theme of the map. Though at times the enemies can feel a little unfair, as Threshers can come out of nowhere to hit you for big damage, Stalkers will hunt you down relentlessly and Spiderants are just plain unavoidable. Though this doesn't retract massively from the excellent gameplay that has been laid down.
Overall, the fighting works well, each character has their own unique quirks and backstory, and every passing line in the game feels as if the characters was actually speaking to you. Again, the humour in this game is fantastic, and aids in setting up the world of Pandora amazingly.

APB:R Is a truly outstanding freemium game, You get the large choice of trying to keep peace and order as an enforcer, or burn, smash and wreck the city San Paro.
This games offers a new level of customization, you cannot only costumize your self, but your cars, clothes, spray, music, and more.
You will be able to enjoy this one of a kind urban freemium game to the max, even if youre a F2P, Because P2P called Premiums ingame, only get 25% bonus on their income from missions and misc, aswell as their reputation.
This game is highly enjoyable with a friend, and there is plently of room to freeroam in the streets and highways of San Paro.
Criminal: Ram storefronts, Mug people, sell cars, deliver goods, or cause a random destruction! A criminal's limits of income is his fear of being witnessed by any enforcer.
Enforcer: Pin down the Criminals as youre slowly stalking them, and as you see they get more and more dirty cash on them you witness them the last secound to take their loot and return it as edvidence for a big reward. As an enforcer youre not "allowed" to drive down neutral npcs nor destroy the enviroment such as a mailbox.
The Graphics: The graphical level of this game is also at its max, you can any time turn them down/off in case your computer sadly cannot run it fully, but everything in this game is beuatyful and highly detailed.
Weapons: You will get a free permanent weapon called  STAR 556 its a lovely riffle, fully automatic and well balenced, as a secondary you get to carry the Obeya FBW, and there is two other ways of gaining new weapons by Leasing or Purchasing from ARMAS(APB:R shop) By leasing a weapon up to 7 days or use a (sadly) large sum of your money on some permanent weapons.
Vehicles:  This i cannot put down good enough but the cars are one of the most enjoyable features in this game! Theyre each very unique and offers a great pleasure as youre driving them around in San Paro, with a friend hanging out of the window or not :)
Enviroment: In the streets of San Paro, you quickly figure out where to stay when youre ramming, or where to stay if youre mugging, and the same for enforcers, many enforcers have their little "route" they travel to see if anyone is witnessable (Means the criminal and enforcer get to battle for the dirty money). San Paro is a beuatyful city offering many wonderful places to visit, either youre at a dark alley runnning for your life, or at a contacts place having a blast.
PVP!: This game is purely based on pvp, but not only do you need to focus on other players against you but also those who are with you because know what? FRIENDLY FIRE IS ON! :D that feature is out of our reach and we will have to deal with it, I am personally loving that feature as the game pushes you even further to take caution for your enviroment.
Overall: This game is far beyond my belief of a good freemium game, but its balanced alot and well done! few for and against
+PVP
+Cars/Enviroment
+Costumization
+Wide amount of weapons be it leased or purchased.
+Open world, freeroam
+Balanced freemium gameplay, no-one is TOO overpowered *cough nano,colby,csg.*

Being someone that grew up on films like Mad Max, Jurassic Park, Terminator, and Monty Python, its easy to say that I'm a giant nerd for a variety of genres. The diesel punk inspired world of Mad Max perfectly captures the look and feel of Fury Road film it was meant to occompany, but also throws back a lot of mentions toward the original films, most prominatly Road Warrior but also some call backs to Beyond Thunderdome. The gameplay is tight and responsive, most notably in the car mechanics. The customization of the car is expansive and allows for many different types of Road Warriors. From those who value t-boning to the pyros who just wanna watch the world burn. All of the characters are memorable, but the real shout out goes to my gunner Chum Bucket, who easily sold the crazy zealout hunchback with a gift with cars. This game took the lore and subtle story elements of Road Warrior, Thunderdome, and Fury Road, and pulled them together, from the term blackfinger mentioned in Fury Road, to the reference to Max being called "The Raggedy Man" and all of the hints to the background of the world and max scattered throughout fully emmerse one in the world of Mad Max.

One of the best Hitman games I've played, possible the best gameplay wise. Story and pacing was the best at Hitman Blood Money, but I feel this game comes a close second on the overall quality.
I do kinda see why they have gone with the episodic format for this game, it fits the game, it fits the Hitman concept, and all the levels are VERY much replayable. You can literally spend up to 10-15 hours on every mission and throughout those hours you will experience a lot of new and previously undiscovered feauteres and content. But I do myself think I would've liked a complete game or at least a full season 1 at launch, and not wait 2 months for a new mission, it does kill the momentum and I feel diminishes interest overall for the game in the general public in the long run. I do hope I'm wrong on that last statement, because I would like this game to do well, it's really a good one!
Finially, the one thing this game definitely lacks is Jesper Kyd for it's soundtrack... That Blood Money OST, oh god, that did SO MUCH for the atmosphere, it was a perfect fit for the game. I hope they will bring him back for season 2.
Recommended for all fans of the series, especially those who were really disappointed with Absolution (I was for one). This game does Hitman really well.

This game takes all the great concepts behind Rocksteady's Batman Franchise and builds on them to improve it even further. The story is interesting and keeps you wanting to play, the detective mode is much more immersive and gets you actually thinking about the crime you are investigating instead of just pressing the button the game wants you to press. I guess the small amount of criticism I have for the game is the combat is a little too over the top. Like Arkham City, Origins just goes too far in the type of combat that batman is capable of and for me that takes me out of the game. I would probably be happy if Batman just couldn't leap 20 feet between every hit, and was constrained to a more human five feet within a combat flow. The great thing about Batman for me is that this is just a guy without super powers, its the struggle that he has to make to do what he does. When he can consistently perform the physically impossible, it just kind of ruins that.

It's a great game if you are into management and building (tycoon) sims.
The only problem which makes the game less appealing is the poor optimization of the game overall, the game fps drops over time as you build and reach ~300 prisoner capacity even on a high end rig. Frame drops can be noticed on less if you build on large maps or buy a few land expansions. Playing on 15-30 fps can be slow and painful to expand further. I mean why have an achievement for 1000 prisoners when the game simply can’t handle it.
If they could fix the optimization issues {which I doubt will happen now), it has a lot of potential.
Overall 7/10

It is with heavy heart I give the thumbs down for this game, as it is better than most games out there, but it must be judged with comparison to the earlier games in the series, and compared to Blood Money, it is nothing.
As most other negative reviews probably discuss, the missions are way too few to call this a complete game. Even though the mission maps themselves are often larger than in the earlier games, they feel bland to me, and the missions objectives in each of them is no more than before, thus the time you spend to complete each mission is not significantly larger than before, meaning that the missions are played through in a breeze.
What I perhaps miss the most from Blood Money, (even the horrendous Absolution), is that the levels in those games contain a lot of hidden things to find in off-the-beaten-path rooms and sometimes humorous dialog between guards. It is hard to explain, but I feel that the levels in Hitman (2016) lack any of this at all, and feel like sterile areas run by a strict government or something. I have thoroughly checked every room in the levels so far, and found very few things of interest.
A lot of angry discussions in the message boards are of the two camps: achievement replayers vs story/silent assassin people. I am in the latter camp, and grinding my way through the same level a hundred times is not for me. Thus, I cannot give this game a good score. The story has also been disappointingly confusing and uninteresting thus far, but I admit that the Hitman games have never really been about the story, even though there is an interesting core framing around most of the earlier releases.

Being someone that grew up on films like Mad Max, Jurassic Park, Terminator, and Monty Python, its easy to say that I'm a giant nerd for a variety of genres. The diesel punk inspired world of Mad Max perfectly captures the look and feel of Fury Road film it was meant to occompany, but also throws back a lot of mentions toward the original films, most prominatly Road Warrior but also some call backs to Beyond Thunderdome. The gameplay is tight and responsive, most notably in the car mechanics. The customization of the car is expansive and allows for many different types of Road Warriors. From those who value t-boning to the pyros who just wanna watch the world burn. All of the characters are memorable, but the real shout out goes to my gunner Chum Bucket, who easily sold the crazy zealout hunchback with a gift with cars. This game took the lore and subtle story elements of Road Warrior, Thunderdome, and Fury Road, and pulled them together, from the term blackfinger mentioned in Fury Road, to the reference to Max being called "The Raggedy Man" and all of the hints to the background of the world and max scattered throughout fully emmerse one in the world of Mad Max.

While there is a lot there for the makings of a good game- fun but simple music, a wacky (slightly offensive) plot, simple game design and the enjoyable feature of a simultaneously replay ( watching an army of Super Meat Boys getting destroyed simultaneously only for one to survive is certainly fascinating) the game is simple not fun. It is not fun for one single reason- it is too damn difficult. Some people might get off on a game that is punishingly difficult. I, on the other hand, can not ever see myself having fun playing the same 10-20 second level for an hour. Over and over and over and over and over again. Even with the funny replay feature it is simple not enough of a jem at the end of this agonizing trial to make it worth it. While the game does avoid long waiting times between replays (no watching the same cut scene again and again here) this is really only a bandage on a far more systemic problem. The human mind can only enjoy anything, even the must fun activity, after only so many repetitions. So for the few of you who enjoy this kind of self punishment I would maybe recommend this a try. For the rest of us  I would recommend you avoid this game.
