Spec Ops: The Line is a very story rich game with a rather deep narrative. If you play it as just another shooter, vaguely paying attention to the characters, your choices and the game's ambiance you can miss out on a lot. This game feels an awful lot like like an 'art movie' ... or similar form of storytelling device where you need to be wide awake and thinking through your choices and the choices of others. What they imply, mean or intend. Are these good choices? Moral choices? Or not? Did you have any other choice?
The above said, It is a modern FPS, military game on rails for the most part. You -will- die a few times, there are no console commands. This is not an open world survival game. But you don't play it for the FPS aspect. That, merely serves as the medium through which the story of the main character is told.  Further, this is a game with a good deal of intellectual, mature, adult concepts. It presents a war-torn environment where humans are flawed, where horrible things have transpired. Where awful choices have been made. Good intentions? Madness? People trying to just survive an environmental catastrophe?
For better or worse the game's story isn't completely linear. There are a couple moments where perspective, and timing are played with for dramatic effect. As a result, it's important to remain alert and conscious of the unfolding story as you play through it. Otherwise you might end up vaguely confused wondering what happened and why, or whether you could have done anything different to change the course of the plot.
In closure, great story. Good game.

Spec Ops: The Line. From all the praise, I was expecting something unique and different. I can't say I got any of that.
Good things first. The setting. Sandstorm weathered Dubai is something truly unique, I can give it that. Skyscrapers buried in sand with the constant threat of storms where civilians and armed forces try to survive is absolutely fresh. The strong glaring sun and bloom, although most of the time very distracting, added to the hot weather feel.
Voice acting was quite nice. Felt pretty good to listen to although some lines were really awkward but that's just the script.
Sand worked quite nicely as a mechanic also, although it kinda died off the further I went on in the game.
Well, the bad things. Let's start with the big praised and awarded morale. Did the game make me feel like a hero? No. Did the game make me feel bad? No. Why? I was wondering, why would it? I was stuck on rails. I went on how the game wanted me to go and suddenly what I did was wrong in the end. But I didn't have much of a choice. It was like reading a book. There was only one outcome. There were a couple choices to be made but I felt like they didn't make much difference. I picked one option and I was told, "Well, that's how things go". There are three different endings but I'll just say nothing you do between start and end matters. I couldn't feel bad for "Wakuhs's" (player character) choices because I couldn't affect his larger choices and I couldn't relate on him at all.
Maybe I was supposed to feel sorry for the characters but the thing was that my squad was "The Bro Delta Squad" kind. I didn't like the fact that I was a superior and my squad could just act like brats because we were such bros. It made me feel annoyed and I wanted to personally end my squad mates. So whatever quarrel we had made me want to slide under the table in shame. The civilians were angry for a good reason but they felt like complete idiots. Our objective at one point was to issue an evacuation order but I felt like I might have missed something. Why haven't the civilians left? That makes them stupid, except the sandstorm keeps them there. So they can't really leave. So why are we trying to tell them to leave in the first place? That makes us stupid. If our solution was to round up some nice vehicles and then escort them but no. Our plan was just to tell them to leave. Tell a bunch of angry mindless civilians to march into their doom.
Gameplay. Clunky, sticky, unresponsive at times. Aiming and shooting was plausible. Running and using cover, awful. Spec Ops: The Line falls under the category of games that handles most things with just one key. Running and taking cover happens from space. However, other things such as vaulting happened from shift. It just didn't feel natural. I felt like cover related actions should've been in one button and movement related in another. On top of it all, my character didn't feel like staying in cover sometimes. He would just pop his head out and refused to take cover. Firefights felt like a chore because the enemy threw grenades with pinpoint accuracy constantly. There were times when they threw grenades through my cover as well. So I couldn't stay in the cover for more than a second or two. I had to retreat away from the fight because I was pretty much as far as I could be from the enemies. Once I returned to the cover, another grenade was lobbed at me. Not really fun. A cover shooter that punishes you for using cover?
tl;dr
Pretty average cover TPS. Morality executed poorly. Clunky controls. Nice story, voice acting and visuals though. Not a super long game. If you enjoy a good story, get it. If you favor gameplay, don't get it.

Update as of 10/11/2016
Hitman has been tremendously updated and there are several factors I can squeal with glee to see have fixed, but there are still issues that plague the game and frustrating AI inconsistancies that drive me absolutely nuts.
First, let me say that it's great to have those annoying crashing bugs fixed, Hitman hasn't crashed on me once in the last few months and that's refreshing because the first thing I love doing is a "stealth kill everyone" run the moment new content comes out. I mean who doesn't? It's fun! This was previously impossible because killing NPCs beyond a certain point would not only crash your game but corrupt all save files including autosaves related to that run, so loading a previous save didn't help much. It was frustrating and killed any joy I had for the game, so it's nice to keep jumping back into the game now and doing what I do best, MURDER!
Server issues are still a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ I, unlike others, don't mind the single player aspect, although I wouldn't complain if there were Co-op options as well. Always online is there to prevent pirates circumventing buying the game, but they also give players a headache when they aren't working consistantly. Fix this! It's frustrating to be playing seriously and have your progress ignored because you weren't online and didn't even realise or the mission just cut off on you.
AI is okay for the most part, but there are still annoying things and confusing things. Voice acting is lazy, I'd like some variety, especially in other countries, even if subtitles are required for translation, immersive-ness and all that. AI being able to see you or your crimes through walls is still an annoying bug that has made me lose many an elusive target mission. I have the perfect set up, I just need to incapacitate two guards and hide in the closet, but what's this? A guard on the floor below me or in the room next to me has seen me and now I'm compromised and hunted? WTF? There's that, and there is also the "seen if you miss a headshot", which is quite frankly ridiculous. Granted, guards would be alerted and come to find out where the source of the gunshot came from, but no, I wasn't seen, nobody saw me fire that shot, that's bull.
On the topic of AI, I'd still like a harder mode introduction. Despite the AI flaws, they can sometimes be a little too relaxed about the accumulating pile of corpses that keep showing up, which unless you are trying to be as perfect as perfection allows, encorages you to be lazy and leave bodies around because you have little fear of being caught or compromised. A survival mode for each of the existing levels would be great, where AI is kicked up a notch, far more alert and investigative when bodies show up and that sense of urgency and emergency only growing the more bodies that they find.
My final gripe is with the venture capitalist style of payment. I don't mind paying per level, gives me something to look forward to each month and had they made this clear in the beginning, consumers wouldn't have been so annoyed with the 2 demos and a single level deal they had when Hitman first came out. Their stance keeps changing however and it can make consumers uneasy. Why should I buy a seasonal pass if you keep changing the terms of what I'm getting? Can you guarantee the £30/40 I spend now will be beneficial in the long run? Can I not just pay per episode you introduce? Why can't I pay for bonus levels separately without buying the overpriced full season and why didn't you warn me this would be the case at the beginning? There's certainly no value for money me paying for a full season just to get bonus levels when I've already bought all the levels separately.
The paid scheme is a mess and there doesn't seem to be much consistancy to it. I assumed that if I were to switch to the full season it would remove the levels I've paid for already from the charge, but it doesn't and that's a con. So warning to all newcomers, buy season pass, or prepare to miss out on bonus content...unless you like to pay through the teeth.
Conclusion:
Bugs are still there, server issues and AI related. Pricing is a mess and it only makes consumers uneasy about what they are getting and whether or not it is worth it.
Gameplay is smoother, cleaner and still enjoyable.

Ultimatly, a rip off. More replay value than actual value.  Each map took me approx. 20 minutes to finish on normal difficulty, with four maps currently out. The game is beatable in under an hour!!!
The levels are large and detailed and have many available options to assassinate an enemy and the story is interesing and well written.  Unfortunatly, all of that is overwritten by the utter lack of content.  once you beat the story the rest of the time you is spent replaying the same map attempting assassination challenges or escalation missions.
The "challenges" are a joke, as most of them are unlocked by simply escaping the map a certain way, or choosing a different starting location within the map (completeing challenges unlocks more starting locations. Starting at the new location is a challenge unlock in and of itself, completing the loop of why ♥♥♥♥ing bother.)
The escalation missions are more or less boring as they have nothing to do with the game, map, or story. The escalation missions require you to assassinate various nobodies on the maps you already completed for the story. Then once you kill that person, you can play the the escalation mission again, and again, and again.... 5 times for each escalation 'mission" (i shouldnt even really call them missions as they are a joke) Each time you complete an escalation mission, the difficulty "escalates", allowing you to replay that mission but with a different tweaks like using a certain disguise, assassinating them a certain way, or adding more people to assassinate.  I understand that the gameplay is based on assassinating people and finding new ways to do it.  But after playing the same map 40 times just to get the achievement or challenge unlocked, you're sick of the map.  You're sick of the game.  You get sick of assassinating a bunch of nobody's at the same damn party with the same damn ways with the same damn goals.  Its tedious, pointless, and an excuse to keep people playing with as minimal content possible.
TL;DR  DONT BUY IT, TOTAL WASTE!  30minutes of gameplay per map, 1 map per episode, 4 episodes released so far and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ prologue you have to play twice.  HOW THE ♥♥♥♥ IS THIS RATED WELL IN STEAM STORE?

Avadon 3 is an epic isometric CRPG. It has a really great story, quite some lore to explore, a world that is unbelievably big and detailed and interesting, turn-based party combat. I've played quite a bit more of the game than the few hours on my account are showing as I got a press pre-release version by the very nice guys from Spiderweb Software.
It is retro and indie, so there is sound but no music yet, the graphics are retro but they have high resolution and detail (HD) available. There is though, a game filled with love. It's just really fun. The Tutorial leads you into the game very well and the interface and quest system is actually really modern and easy to use. The urge to explore and find more in this action-, treasure and lore-laden world soon gets you and then you're on the hook. Like I am now!
At the start, you get sent out on missions and you can choose to take characters that you've met before with you. You have total control over them and also manage their attributes, skills and equipment. It is based on the mission how many people you can take with you, at the start you got your main character and a blademaster, a shadowwalker (some kind of thief/ninja) and a sorcerer at your disposal.
You can watch game footage in my Let's Play where I'm adding episodes three times a week. But the start should already show you most. In episode three you can see how the combat works, too.

Leaving the original review unaltered below, adding some updated thoughts now that I've had time to play it more...  The story and dialogue is still as excellent as I remember in past games, so I'm just going to talk about the mechanics / battles.
Vogel always iterates his system every game, and now that I've had a chance to actually get into some of the battles I'll list a few things I'm enjoying as improvements or haven't managed to update from previous Avadon titles:
+ Mana is no longer something that you just chink away at slowly and occasionally forces you to go touch a healing pylon.  Instead your mana is an actual resource in fights that returns fairly immediately after fights.  I enjoy this more from a tactical perspective, he's learned a lot that many gamers don't enjoy the survival / bar management style of things and is focusing on immediate battle stuff.
+ Hard mode adds friendly fire.  I'm not sure if it also adds friendly fire to the enemies or they have it naturally, but this is a good addition to making hard mode more difficult and strategic without the 'raw numbers' problem that's occasionally plagued his earlier games.
+ Taunting actually seems to work right on Blademasters finally.
= Graphics are largely unchanged.  This doesn't bother me, but don't look for graphical powerhouse here.  Still, for a retro-style game I think everything looks fairly polished.
- Shops are still as worthless as they have been in every game.  Money is still extremely useful to buy permanent boosts or extremely potent items that are scattered towards the endgame, but spending any money in the basic shops is just a trap that will penalize you later on.
Stil an overall very strong buy for any fans of turn based tactical combat, strong storylines, and choices with non-immediate effects that matter.
-- ORIGINAL REVIEW --
I haven't had time to fully get into this game, so this is just a preliminary review.
If you haven't played any of Spiderweb Software's Avadon games before:  The brief rundown is that you're going to create a noob character of one of five available classes and pick up controllable NPCs of each of the five other available classes with their own personalities / stories.  You still retain full control over the leveling / skill ups of the NPCs.
Battles can be done in four difficulty levels, I'm trudging through on Hard with what I feel is an appropriate level of difficulty.  You can change at any time, preventing a difficulty spike from making you want to rage at the game unable to progress.  Combat's turn based and very tactical, with most standard fights keeping to predictable mechanics and spells equivalent to what your party members have, and boss fights often like puzzles.
Vogel's writing has been honed fairly well over the years, it's often wryly humorous.  If you don't enjoy reading a lot, you might want to stay away, a large joy in the Avadon games is in the extensive plot and your personal reactions to the plights of the people in the gameworld.  That said, I still think there's a lot to get out of purely the tactical combat if that's your cup of tea.
Having played all his games and the prior Avadon ones, I see some streamlining of things from the prior games but most of it is recognizable.  If you like small group tactical RPG action and a strong emphasis on story, his Avadon games are a good series to start with.  They're not as deeply customizable as the recent Avernum remakes, which can be both good and bad.  It's almost impossible to screw up your characters in Avadon, but there's only so much different you can do with them as well.
I'll try to edit this with further thoughts when I can play more, but my first hourish with the game is making me look forward to what's going to start happening.

I think it's worth noting that while I DID receive this game to do coverage of it, I have also bought all other titles from Spiderweb Software, whether on Steam or elsewhere.  I'm a geniune fan of Spiderweb Software's work, and my review will reflect that.  :)
I'll keep this short.  Here is my over all thoughts on Avadon 3: The Warborn.
Avadon 3: The Warborn is a fantastic cRPG.  The story is fantastic, you get immersed in it and are always wanting more.  Character progression, combat, exquipment, and exploration are all done to perfection.  Another big thing is the branching storylines, allowing your choices to dictate the ending.  This is an amazing entry into the cRPG genre and definitely deserves some love.
A game that does so many things right, there is very little for me to knitpick.  There are only 3 things I would have liked to see added that didn't make it into the game.
1.  I love the option to play at different resolutions, but I would love a zoom feature too.  That has been my only "gripe" from all of Spiderweb Software's games.  I want just a little bit of zoom every now and then.  At 1080p, it's a bit too far back.  This is fixed by playing at 720p or other resolutions, still..I long for a zoom.
2.  Keybindings.  You can rebind almost all of the keys in Avadon 3, but you can't set your camera movement.  (If you can, I'm blind and didn't see it).  If I could rebind camera movement in addition the what is already offered, Happy Bumpy!
3.  Sound control. Again, all of these "complaints" are super small unimportant things.  I would like a little bit more control over the different sounds in the game.  They did add a normal, off, and quiet mode for the music, but I'd prefer like a 0-10 scale or even 0-5 or something.  Also Sound FX, ambient, or the like.  Just a BIT more control would be nice.
All that being said, those things I mentioned are insignificant little nothings when you consider how flawed some games are.  I 100% highly recommend Avadon 3: The Warborn, and all of Spiderweb Software's RPG library to any RPG fan.  It's old school, it's amazingly well done, and it deserves praise.

Batman Arkham Origins Review
Being a fan of the Arkham Asylum and City I couldn't wait for this game to come out. Sadly the game was a massive failure to the Arkham franchise, never had I waited for a game to end more than this. In the 17 or so hours it took for me to complete the game, half the time Arkham City took I might add, I experienced roughly the same systems in place as the first two with little changes to the formula other than a game breaking weapon given late game, numerous QTEs and a massive amount cinematic sequences. This game had so much going for it coming from a fantastic couple of preceding games but takes the name and combat system alone and adds nothing but boredom to the equation. Many of the assassins battles are more spectacle than substance and lack the punch the earlier games had going for them. The cinematics, while good looking, merely add to the length of the game with few even necessary to the narrative as a whole. The most troubling of the additions are the numerous quick time events. These make portions of the game feel "press-to-win" especially when the majority of them are in the games most desperate situations. There are several graphical and system bugs in the game as well which make it visually unappealing during some of the most enjoyable parts including one of my favorite features of the series gliding high above the city streets. The game also often crashes on exiting the game and the controls seem less responsive which makes combat seem like a gamble of timing more than a show of skill. Something was lost in the series between changing developers and it has suffered a great blow. This installment is not worthy of the series and I am truly glad to say that it is not a necessity  to play or even own.

I wish I could give this game a recommended rating but sadly I just can't. I got this game the day it came out, was super hyped and admittedly there are a lot of good features in this game! However the dev team truly seems to care more about avoiding PR then thier fans or even this game. Regardless here's my comparision lists:
Pros:
-Great music, graphics and writting! Everything is very cohesive and it just feels very refined. Not only is the story (both chosen and required) very well written for most routes but the different features just look amazing and modern.
-Replayability, coming back to this game to replay a few parts was really fun due to the fact that this game is pretty well put together (in some regards).
-Customization in terms of different dialogue options and character appearance makes you really feel like you're apart of the game, I love little touches like that and this game hit them right on the head.
-Cute gay dads! The dates you go on are usually very good, the characters have a lot of personality and playing through each of their stories to learn more is rewarding (in most cases).
-Minigames! A few of these fall flat but even the simpler ones where you don't really do anything are funny and atmospherically enjoyable.
Cons:
-The story is incomplete. When I first got this game the day it came out I could make excuses for the messy ending and seemingly anticlimatic over arching plot that this game presents when you go through one of the character's routes. It drove me crazy but I waited for an answer. Still, there are none. You can look in the coding/public forums but this game literally has a whole section that is unaccessible (and that will probably never be correctly coded into the game due to the potential bad PR) and that is objectively vital to the storyline they were setting up. Once you know about it the game makes sense, you realize there are so many eastereggs hidden in the game for it. Sadly they chose not to include it in the game which sets you up for fustration and disaapointment.
-Glitches; yes they have fixed a lot of these and honestly most of them are just weird/don't take away from the game for something that costs 15 dollars, has as much hype as it does and has been out for so long they shouldn't be there any more.
-In contrast to what I said above, some minigames are just too flat to be completely enjoyable, alot of people don't like the dad creator since the style is 100% different from every other sprite in the game and alot of people are fustrated by the lack of content. In my opinion there was a good amount but other people dislike how you only got 3 dates with each dad (which is probably actually a testimony to how good this game is).
Regardless I like the game it is kinda fun but if you aren't already a fan don't get sucked in. It's not worth the heartbreak when you realize the story is incomplete even if it has a lot of good features.

"SpecOps: The Line" is a succesful reinstalment of a serie that fell from grace after promising begginings. "The Line" leaves behind realism and goes for action TPS with tactical elements. And does the job just fine.
When it comes to technicals and mechacnics, "SpeOps: The Line" is just another, cover-based, generic TPS. It looks good, sounds good, plays good. But nothing mindblowing. Higher difficulty levels means more HP for your enemies and less for you. Playing on hard means your enemies will be quite a bullet sponge while FUBAR makes the game a bit tiring as great majority of levels has poor rail-design. It does improve but too late - when you come to the point where you can do some maneuvering and commanding you teammates makes some sense, you will be just few steps from finishing the game. But, to give credit they deserve - fighting in those locations is very interesting and exciting - pity the devs did not put such an effort earlier. Also, issuing commands is unintuitive. So I'd keep to normal difficulty to get the best from the game.
The plot and narrative is where the game shines. You wouldn't be far from thruth saying thet "The Line" is computer adaptation of Conrad's "Heart of Darkness". It's a story about duty, honor, surviving, doing what's right and what's needed - the story about preserving your humanity. The game probes the 4th wall as the prrotagonist - and indirectly player himself - faces morally challanging situation and is being asked some uncomfrotable questions. Questions you may not like the answers when the time comes. And the grand finale gives completly new look at already interesting plot and available solutions.
So to make the long story short - "SpecOps: The Line" is a good shooter with great story, definietly worth playing and I will be looking forward for any future "SpecOps" titles.

Hitman is back on form.
Now, firstly - Don't bother with the Intro Pack, you're just wasting your time. Get the Full Experience or go home, Valve give you 2 hours before you can get a refund, use it.
Now, the content...
Levels are all a giant sandbox, the entire selling point of the game is in the replay value of the maps - whether that's devising new and creative ways to kill the target(s) or engaging in the online content and periodic "Elusive Targets" that are made available. Level design has shown to be very ambitious with plenty to enjoy and explore.
The developers have shown to be reasonably responsive to community feedback in terms of making quality-of-life improvements to the user interface. The game also does not dictate how you play it: leave all the help options on or turn them off for added challenge. It won't net you a higher score, however and the leaderboards are entirely a matter of speedrunning which can be enjoyable to some, not so much for others. Fortunately, said leaderboards are purely bragging rights.
The weakest point of the game is the contract creation system which, whilst it has gone through significant improvement, it's still relatively unsatisfying since the ways in which the contract creator eliminated their selected targets are basically optional to anyone else who carries it out. Nonetheless, playing the player created contracts and honouring their way of completion is still good fun.
If you enjoyed Blood Money or you like sandbox-like games where their raison d'etre is being stealthy and replaying levels, you'll like this game.

APB: Reloaded has gone downhill significantly since it's Free-to-Play release. While it still retains a good feeling for the gunplay mechanics, the prevelance and overzealous pushing of the cash shop along with annoying players with "subscribe now!" advertisements tends to get in the way.
Over time weapons have been tuned in such a way that significant advantages (especially in lower threat levels and ranks) are outright purchasable with real cash, and these aren't cheap. Permanent weapons can cost upwards of a full $40 if not more, but at least now they're able to be applied to all characters on an account for a premium.
Cheating is a very common problem these days, be it via hacks or gaming the threat/matchmaking system. With no real appropriate ladder, and the overwhelming amount of people who feel that if they aren't winning they aren't having fun; we find that more and more players will use every and any trick in the book and out of the book to win with illegitimate results.
If you can get over those issues though, and play APB:R without too much invested in  it with a few friends, you can have an absolute blast be it chasing down criminal players or resisting arrest from enforcers.
The question here is whether or not APB:R is good enough to warrant still being alive, and that's a debatable answer.

Euro Truck Simulator 2;
As you can tell from the name, it's a simulator. Let's just start this review off by saying, simulators are not for everyone. In Euro Truck Simulator 2 you take the wheel of a tractor trailer across Europe. You start your own trucking company and make deliveries. As you progress the distance gets longer and the money you make increases. Honestly, this is one of the best simulator games around. It's a great way to just sit back, relax and pass the time peacefully. Nobody is yelling at eachother like in multiplayer games. The only thing you have to worry about is keeping your truck in its lane, not hitting other cars/trucks and stopping for red lights. I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who loves driving games and who maybe looking to get into simulators.
Pros:
-Great Time Passer
-Good Graphics
-Very Realistic
-You Drive All Across Europe
-Learn How to Manage Your Own Company
Cons:
-There is none, buy this game.
Final Verdict:

1.) It had an ending.

This is a really nice Dating Sim. Granted, it's the second one I've played, but I do really think this is nice. The only improvements I could say are to fix those minor glitches that makes everyone mad and maybe add more story onto the game. DLC, perhaps? All in all, this game is definitely worth the money. The stories are really nice, and I've just fallen in love with all the characters and the game in general.

Pros:
- Nice, cutesy writing.
- Dad puns galore.
- Amanda (your daughter) is a hoot. Also I feel like this is much better equpped to be a parenting sim than a dating sim, because she is by far the most intresting and fleshed-out character, but this might just be a matter of taste.
Cons:
- I'm gonna say it. The dad creator sucks. Your character always ends up looking too cartoony which contrasts horribly to all the well drawn and fleshed out characters in the game. I restarted at least 3 times becuase I couldn't bear how horrible my character looked compared to others.
- The mini games are disjointed from the game. Differnt art style, different controls, no explanation on what you are supposed to do - and to top it off not much of an effect on anything what so ever.
- The content doesn't justify the price like...at all. The art is minimal, there are a few backgrounds, the same character models are used for each situation and each of your love intrests gets 1 gallery entry upon the completion of their romance. This makes the game somewhat tedious to play because it might as well be a choose your own adventure book with the pictures of the characters for reference at the beginning. It just doesn't add much. In other games I've payed for a similar price range there would be complete galleries of unlockables or each character as well as different scenes for the game as a whole. 5 bucks tops is what I would recoommend you pay for this game.
- The story is not well put together. Unlike other visual novels I've played where there is a main story line where your choices determine at the end which ending you get, here the story - between you and your daughter - is merely a bythought and is dealt wih after your first 2-3 dates with guys. And after that you are free to go through all the dads and date them with no sense of story or linearity. Not to mention that their content is a measly 2+1 dates spread over a few days (weeks? this game also has no semblence of time passing) which hardly seems like the amount of time you would fall in love with someone.

It's a great game and all don't get me wrong but that's all it is. Nothing more nothing less. I've played this game for around 5 hours and to be completely honest it's really not worth it. (unless you're completely obsessed with dating and daddies)
I'd say keep the money and look around for something better because at the end of the day all this is, is basically a choose your own adventure. Lot's of reading too and something that a true wattpad lover would enjoy. But just not for me.

Let's get this out of the way-- I absolutely LOVED this game. It's cardinal sin in my opinion is that there just wasn't enough of it. Am I supposed to plausibly believe that your MC could fall in love with their Daddy of choice in three dates?
Daddies, take a good look at the MC. As much as they touted a customizable character, the creator was just an absolute joke-- which I suppose, is what they were going for. Personally, I would have accepted if the MC was at the very least drawn in a similar style. AT LEAST make it look like they come from the same universe!
And then there's the bugs. (EDIT: Removed the bugs I listed as I've been made aware that there has been a patch from September. Sorry about that!) I have no clue, but I haven't received an update to this game since god knows when, and it makes me think the devs stopped giving a crap because everyone had already given them their money.
Look, I play games like this a LOT. Sure, most are erotic and will not be everyone's cup of tea, but those games are absolutely beautiful. The production, the music, the voice acting (FULL voice acting like on the tin instead of a cacophony of grunts that you have to fast forward through everytime you repeat an event, which, if you're like me and played every single route at least twice for each ending, had to do a lot), hell, the art was better! More CGs than you could shake a stick at instead of having a half hearted sketch at the end of the route. (Did you just spend two hours trying to finish Brian's mini golf game perfectly? HERE, just ONE picture. Don't get me wrong, it was one of the better ending CGs in the game. I was massively let down by Damian's and Joseph's-- who were two of my favorites.)  Even the MCs of THOSE games had voice acting (Take Drammatical Murder, or if you want a more recent title, NO, THANK YOU!!!. Yes, they're Adult only games valued at twice what DDADDs is, but a fan of this genre who is coming from these titles and to DDaDDs will probably draw comparisons and be disappointed.)
TL;dr: Are you a fan of the Grumps and maybe want to support a small developer's first stab at a game? Sure, get it. Are you a vet at these visual novel style games and figure you can get your money's worth from this cute title? Find it cheaper somewhere else and save up your money for a different game, you'll thank me.

This game is as Mad Max-y as anything anyone could have envisioned.  ALL of the grit, the gas, the horsepower, the brutality, really it's all there.  And if you're like me and you haven't been burnt out on Arkham Asylum's combat (granted it's a bit of a watered down version), when you're not having a blast in your truly authentic Mad Max vehicles, you'll be running around brutalizing a bunch of bad fellows face to face rather than car to face.
It's not perfect.  I can't say that.  But I had a great deal of fun and did a good bit of the ridiculous amount of extraneous content in the game.   The story won't wow you and the gameplay can get repetitive, but you can really feel the effort put in to making Mad Max look, feel, and sound like what you'd imagine a post-apocalyptic dystopia of rusted steel, sand, and gasoline would really be like.  Engines roar, explosions are dense and pack a punch, metal grinds and whines as it bends and breaks... it's just a treat for the senses and really begs for bigger monitors (thank you Big Picture mode) and loud speakers.
To put it in a nutshell, it's well worth the tiny price it often goes on sale for.  Even though it lacks the great potential it had for DLC content, you're going to get some enjoyable hours out of this if anything you've read here sounds remotely appealing.
I know a lot of people love this game, but it just does not do it for me in any way. Playing it feels like a chore not a pleasure.

This has to be the most challenging platform game I’ve ever played; Super Meat Boy  (SMB) rises steadily in difficulty from easy to ridiculously hard core crazy.  After passing the first boss I had to stop simply because my tired old bones and aching hands were almost suffering from RSI .  That said; this is a beautifully executed game that will keep the   most dedicated of platformer fans wanting more.
SMB has an endearing  style of its own  (despite the copious  trails and splashes of blood with precisely  designed levels that  fit the theme of the game perfectly, plus  it takes me back to  the days when skill was   the most important  attribute for getting through  a level.  You'll need lots of that if you are to get to the   end of this game, especially unscathed.  I really don't know how anyone could get through a complete area without dying at least once.  You'd need to be superhuman, or   one of the best platformers in the world to beat   these levels.
You'll  often be  surprised or even relieved  at how short  some of the levels are (no more than about  30 seconds); that said, with a content of over 300 maps, bonus stages and hidden warp zones  that contain challenging extra-maps,  dark worlds (one for each stage, e.g. Salt Factory Dark World, Hell Dark World etc)  and,  not forgetting  the unlock-able characters which can be gained by collecting bandages that are placed in hard to get locations on several levels or   finishing warp zones - try getting through one of   the  main  stages or the hidden  dark worlds without dying to gain  achievements -  only  0.6% to 1% of the Meat boy community are  getting these achievements because they are ultra hard to  achieve.  Anyway, with all of these  extra's plus  using the editor, (which you'll find in your library under tools),  you have the potential to create unlimited  levels, that are only limited by your imagination, need for more levels  and stamina,  it's hard to get bored of this game. On top of that you're able to implement Maps made by the community.
If you don't already own SMB; now that its over 3 years old, you'll easily pick it up for a bargain price, especially in the many Steam sales that we get these days.
I highly recommend this game, despite me not  achieving much in the way of completing most of the levels  yet , (I've spent over 20 hours playing this game already and I'm still hungry for more)   nor getting  many of the in game achievements (couldn't be bothered  collecting the bandages, lol).  I certainly intend returning to the game when my hands have recovered from the deviously  executed level designs.
If you've not played this game  get it as soon as you can; maybe check out the demo (unfortunately Steam don't offer a demo download), or play the browser  based   flash game:
to get a feel for the game.
Highly recommended and  a 9 out of 10 from me (it loses a point simply because  its a little too hard for me.
Last words:  It's one of the best platformers of the last decade in my opinion (apart from maybe Gish).

This is the Hitman we needed after Blood Money, not Absolution.
I was worried about this game at first due to it being episodic but with 4 episodes out now, I can safely say this is one of the, if not THE, best games in the Hitman series.
It's improved so much gameplay wise and graphically, very similar to Blood Money with some gameplay elements and improvements from Absolution.
Pros:
-Wide open maps consisting of hundreds of NPCs and filled with creative areas to sneak around
-multiple paths in these maps
-multiple ways to kill a target, including kills that make it seem like accidents
-AI is improved
-Stealth is back where Absolution had lost it for action style gameplay
-The UI is extremely clean and nice to look at. Many options to customize the UI as well.
-The game is absolutely gorgeous
-high replayability and updated content on the regular.
-This game will have more episodes after the first season. A second season and a third season are planned for this game. Hopefully more afterwards but that means for 60 dollars, you're buying a massive game. 2-3 games in one.
-Save anytime system
Cons:
-The PC version needs more optimization, massive amounts of npc or even trees will dip your fps below 30 at times, even at lowered settings with a beastly setup
-If you plan on buying the game one mission at a time, you will be missing out on exclusive content even though you will be technically be paying more than 60 dollars after season one is done. BUY THE FULL GAME, IT'S WORTH IT.
-Always Online, you will be kicked from the game if you lose connection to servers.
-Unable to customize weapons
-Few times dialogue will cut out for a moment (a bug that hasn't been completely fixed yet.)
Overall, this game is absolutely wonderful. With more optimization to the PC version I can see this game getting a massive amount of positive reivews more so than it is now. Don't let the "mixed" overall label fool you, maybe of that comes from early on when the game only had one mission out.
If you can buy the full game and deal with an unoptimizaed game for the time being, this is definitely worth getting especially if you love the Hitman series. If this game continues to rack up positive reviews and sell well, we can probably expect even more seasons for this game. The game looks great enough for them to build on for years.
If you loved Blood Money, stealth and planning your way of assassinating your target(s), this is the game for you.
Note: This game DOES take place after Absolution. It's not a reboot or a prequel. Only the beginning training missions (2 of them) are a prequel to the story, everything afterwards takes place after Absolution's storyline.
Takes Hitman back to its roots.

text:
First and foremost, this is an "adventure" game. No, not an "adventure game." In those you pick up a stick shaped like an "F" and use it to open an oversized lock on a chest full of bubblegum that you'll soon need to throw at some dogs so you can sneak past them to get to the... no. This is an "adventure" game. The game is an adventure.
A real adventure. Like when you take a shortcut through the wilderness, but end up further and further off path as you follow a stream, looking for a good place to cross.
A real adventure. Like when you go hiking in the mountains and get lost. Only to realize it'll be quicker to get back to civilization by continuing forward, rather than returning the way you came.
A real adventure. Like when you find yourself some place you've never been before, and with just a few tools, build yourself a makeshift home and defend it from zombies at night while exploring the world around you during the day. Eventually working your way underground into chasms filled with treasure and the occasional abandoned dwelling. Perhaps running across a giant beehive in an underground jungle or a buried pyramid under the desert. Finding your way deep into the darkness where the dead wander freely and mushrooms fluoresce brightly. Going deeper and deeper yet; to the point where the molten core of the planet lights up your eyes in a way only the sun had previously done.
The hard part of writing a review for a game like this is not spoiling too much while still letting people know how deep the game actually is. So much of what I enjoyed about my first playthrough of this game was discovery. Terraria might seem too simple when you first start out, and then possibly even overwhelming. But you'll be glad you spent effort to follow the stream or continue forward through the mountains.
There's weapons and magic, but you never pick a class, like warrior or archer. Due to the wide range of weapons, accessories, and armor choices you'll suddenly realize at some point, perhaps when surrounded by your minions, that you've specialized as a summoner. Or that you're a wizard, or explosives expert. Or perhaps you're some unique archer-warrior hybrid. But your choices and discoveries have slowly lead you into your role; you never chose it from a drop down list.
There's a multitude of biomes to discover. Each with their own unique enemies, and of course, epic boss fights. There's an incredible number of things you can do as you progress through the game. And while it plays fine single player, if you have a friend or two you can bring with you on this journey, you'll have that much more fun and they will thank you for it.
Sure, you can spend hours upon hours building elaborate castles decorated with furniture you've crafted or statues you've collected from around the world. You can reshape the terrain around you - spreading biomes you like or cutting down those you don't. You can even bring biomes up from deep in the earth and set up the perfect potion mushroom farm right next to your base. One of my favorite things to do is to use the wiring system to set elaborate boobie traps around my fortifications. But you don't have to do any of that to progress. It's really all up to you. Although even if none of that is "your thing," you might be so drawn in that you find yourself happily engaged in such activities.
And yes, a big part of the game is digging, but it's primarily a means of exploration. A means of reaching that next treasure chest, or cluster of gems. A means of reaching the next deep fissure in the earth. A great adventure awaits you.

Oh jeez, where to begin...
It takes a certain kind of gamer, with a decent amount of patience, to enjoy CS:GO. Playing casual or deathmatch is usually fun, and not too stressful or boring or anything because you can always join or quit, and it's more fast-paced and less strategic.
Competitive, on the other hand...
If you are going to play competitive, at least listen in on the voice chat (this is very useful, trust me). Get an autoexec file set up in your configs to set up some buy keybinds and to adjust your settings so they will always be how you like them. This is pretty much required to be somewhat useful. Prepare to be kicked from your first few competitive matches because you have no or only a few kills. Try not to create hate or be annoying, it just makes the community more toxic and will also get you kicked. Comp play is somewhat slow-paced, and you are locked into a match regardless of whether you want to stay or not. You will get yelled at and maybe kicked if you miss an important shot, aren't fast enough doing something, or generally aren't being a good teammate. You will get accused of hacking because you hit a single good shot, and the other team will refuse to kick their blatant spinbot hacker because he's helping them win. So if you can avoid getting mad, you will probably like this. There are plenty of tutorials to help you get good at gameplay, and a lot actually do help, but for casual gamers, it largely come down to patience and control. For me... it's a meh. I don't really like comp, but I will do a match or two a day just for xp and a chance to get my rank up. Casual gamemodes and even vs bots at times are more my cup of tea. But overall, if you're on the fence, just get it. It's cheap and ubiquitous, and something everyone has a story about.

"Meat is animal flesh that is eaten as food. Humans are omnivorous, and have hunted and killed animals for meat since prehistoric times. The advent of civilization allowed the domestication of animals such as chickens, sheep, pigs and cattle, and eventually their use in meat production on an industrial scale.
Meat is mainly composed of water and protein, and is usually eaten together with other food. It is edible raw, but is normally eaten after it has been cooked and seasoned or processed in a variety of ways. Unprocessed meat will spoil within hours or days. Spoilage is caused by the practically unavoidable infection and subsequent decomposition of meat by bacteria and fungi, which are borne by the animal itself, by the people handling the meat, and by their implements.
Meat consumption varies worldwide, depending on cultural or religious preferences, as well as economic conditions. Vegetarians choose not to eat meat because of ethical, economic, environmental, religious or health concerns that are associated with meat production and consumption.
Most often, meat refers to skeletal muscle and associated fat and other tissues, but it may also describe other edible tissues such as offal. Conversely, meat is sometimes used in a more restrictive sense – the flesh of mammalian species (pigs, cattle, lambs, etc.) raised and prepared for human consumption, to the exclusion of fish and other seafood, poultry and other animals."

Disclaimer: by the time im doing this review i should be PARTIALLy drunk , since i mixed Pepsi and Whiskey... but i should be "sober" enough to give you my opinion in this game , it's some sort of challenge... ANYWAY, This review is serious, and SPOILERS FREE.
My brother let me play this game through his library, at first never got into it at all... it seemed a basic military shooter game, and i stopped it for a variety of reasons... but months later i came back with the help of a close friend library sharing, i must say that i took the game again when some friends spoiled me ( a bit) of what happened and why this game has been praised in the internet for its narrative, when i took the rail again, the game was in the highest point of the cliff in the story... and i shall be thankful i made it to see it.
Storywise the game is actually cool, the characters are deep, the situations are really exciting, meditative, and even "scary" of some sort, I must say that once you REALLY investigate the spoilers - story part of the game( I DONT RECOMMEND YOU TO DO THIS , PLAY IT ), and you play it or even replay it. you'll see that this game IS in fact Some sort of mix between The Others and Funny games. (scary)
I must say that i'll focus very much on the story and how i felt since its pretty much what this game is. The game is a mix of the 4th wall type of movie i mentioned early, it really tries to make you see the "horrors of war" and the same time "your guiltyness", Explained furthermore? simple, the game is gonna try to make you see what the real horror of war, or well the pointless fact of killing for the sake of kill, it makes you think about the dark side of games like MOH, COD, BF, and the lack of deepness of those games in those "little details" aspect, because this game spits on the Americanism, Heroism, and Pointless killing in War Games.
The game will try to make you feel bad about war games "violence" or mindless killing but... to be honest i never felt it that way... Not because i'm a crazed psycho murder, but because the game is basically some type of "funny games" film videogame, it will try to make you feel bad about the events that happen in the story. I think the game is emphatized to see why the protagonist is doing wrong, how a normal military mission or order can turn black, that it's not just follow orders and comply, that sometimes things MAY get darker, can go bad, and all of that stuff... I never felt guilty for playing this game like the developers said a long time ago in interviews, shocked yes, but not guilty.
Summarized: the game is Shadow of the Colossus (A some sort of personal travel of ourselves with the protagonist) mixed with the films Funny games (morality of being the spectator/player) and The Others (once you see the story and all the elements, you may want to replay the game/film to see ALL the missing details). This game shall be taken as a some sort of critique war games , and/or different narrative point from videogames, rather than something beyond. This game has a lot of debate and my opinion has been said in this review, you should play it if you wanna see more.
When i finished it i really read a lot of articles of opinion about it and i think it was really cool, because this game still as of today is a little debate about the game meanings, even, debates about events regarding the story and narrations( check em when you finish game).
I'll just say the mayor PRO of this game is the story regardless of what's your opinion about the twists and all of that ( please play it for the story PAY A LOT OF ATTENTION TO IT), so i'll skip to the pro and cons related to this game for finishing this review.
+The Soundtrack is Plausible at best, listing it as a pro since very few tracks and the scary parts of the story made it worth for me.
+ The gameplay is not new, in fact, is so Gears of Warish that at the beginning i felt it a direct copy of regular TPS... But i don't mind eating the same food, as long if it tastes the same or better, so , saying it this way, the gameplay is so comfortable that i really didn't mind it after a while.
+ The voice acting is good.
+ The Coop part of the game seems interesting, can't talk about network problems since that's in my area but it's good, you cant play the campaign in coop but some missions are good for getting some bit of hours.
+ The games has optimization options and customization.
+ Achievements are not that hard to get, and you'll get awarded by doing good efforts, i really liked this style ( but not that it shall be applied to all games, calm down, for this game is good)
+ Good ambient and concepts.
- Havent played the MP, but the MP is so bland in my opinion( seen it on gameplays) that i think its worth to play it only if you are bored. ( i don't know if as of today starting 2016 is populated), this is a SP game with coop missions, and should stay that way.
- Very difficult and frustrating parts of the game, the checkpoints are sometimes very useless and you might get killed by heavy armored guys or snipers or anything you can't take down immediatly, I don't know if this was intended to be done on purpose but it REALLY frustrated me.
- The controls are comfortable but sometimes you'll get ♥♥♥♥ed up by the commands , since the cover system may ♥♥♥♥ up and you can get killed by anything, kinda applying the previous point... if you're playing in higher difficults you will INDEED die from stupid moves from your enemies ( fail nades, enemy you thought it was dead or was hidden all the time, your head showed up a little in the cover... etc), dying from stupid moves WILL happen to you a lot.
- The melee system of the game is really OP, and at the same time is just plain blind, i think there was an achievement for this , i got it i think but there weren't a lot of situations that i used it much, only in executions and sometimes i wanted to save bullets.
- The weapon and ammo system are sometimes incoherent, YES i know they are scarce because of the game ambient but sometimes it just punishes you. although this point might be subjetive.
Opinion Summary:
Get it, play it, read all the articles about the story ( good or bad), and think how the game made you feel... Just that. GL HF.

This is the Hitman we needed after Blood Money, not Absolution.
I was worried about this game at first due to it being episodic but with 4 episodes out now, I can safely say this is one of the, if not THE, best games in the Hitman series.
It's improved so much gameplay wise and graphically, very similar to Blood Money with some gameplay elements and improvements from Absolution.
Pros:
-Wide open maps consisting of hundreds of NPCs and filled with creative areas to sneak around
-multiple paths in these maps
-multiple ways to kill a target, including kills that make it seem like accidents
-AI is improved
-Stealth is back where Absolution had lost it for action style gameplay
-The UI is extremely clean and nice to look at. Many options to customize the UI as well.
-The game is absolutely gorgeous
-high replayability and updated content on the regular.
-This game will have more episodes after the first season. A second season and a third season are planned for this game. Hopefully more afterwards but that means for 60 dollars, you're buying a massive game. 2-3 games in one.
-Save anytime system
Cons:
-The PC version needs more optimization, massive amounts of npc or even trees will dip your fps below 30 at times, even at lowered settings with a beastly setup
-If you plan on buying the game one mission at a time, you will be missing out on exclusive content even though you will be technically be paying more than 60 dollars after season one is done. BUY THE FULL GAME, IT'S WORTH IT.
-Always Online, you will be kicked from the game if you lose connection to servers.
-Unable to customize weapons
-Few times dialogue will cut out for a moment (a bug that hasn't been completely fixed yet.)
Overall, this game is absolutely wonderful. With more optimization to the PC version I can see this game getting a massive amount of positive reivews more so than it is now. Don't let the "mixed" overall label fool you, maybe of that comes from early on when the game only had one mission out.
If you can buy the full game and deal with an unoptimizaed game for the time being, this is definitely worth getting especially if you love the Hitman series. If this game continues to rack up positive reviews and sell well, we can probably expect even more seasons for this game. The game looks great enough for them to build on for years.
If you loved Blood Money, stealth and planning your way of assassinating your target(s), this is the game for you.
Note: This game DOES take place after Absolution. It's not a reboot or a prequel. Only the beginning training missions (2 of them) are a prequel to the story, everything afterwards takes place after Absolution's storyline.
Takes Hitman back to its roots.

First and foremost, this is an "adventure" game. No, not an "adventure game." In those you pick up a stick shaped like an "F" and use it to open an oversized lock on a chest full of bubblegum that you'll soon need to throw at some dogs so you can sneak past them to get to the... no. This is an "adventure" game. The game is an adventure.
A real adventure. Like when you take a shortcut through the wilderness, but end up further and further off path as you follow a stream, looking for a good place to cross.
A real adventure. Like when you go hiking in the mountains and get lost. Only to realize it'll be quicker to get back to civilization by continuing forward, rather than returning the way you came.
A real adventure. Like when you find yourself some place you've never been before, and with just a few tools, build yourself a makeshift home and defend it from zombies at night while exploring the world around you during the day. Eventually working your way underground into chasms filled with treasure and the occasional abandoned dwelling. Perhaps running across a giant beehive in an underground jungle or a buried pyramid under the desert. Finding your way deep into the darkness where the dead wander freely and mushrooms fluoresce brightly. Going deeper and deeper yet; to the point where the molten core of the planet lights up your eyes in a way only the sun had previously done.
The hard part of writing a review for a game like this is not spoiling too much while still letting people know how deep the game actually is. So much of what I enjoyed about my first playthrough of this game was discovery. Terraria might seem too simple when you first start out, and then possibly even overwhelming. But you'll be glad you spent effort to follow the stream or continue forward through the mountains.
There's weapons and magic, but you never pick a class, like warrior or archer. Due to the wide range of weapons, accessories, and armor choices you'll suddenly realize at some point, perhaps when surrounded by your minions, that you've specialized as a summoner. Or that you're a wizard, or explosives expert. Or perhaps you're some unique archer-warrior hybrid. But your choices and discoveries have slowly lead you into your role; you never chose it from a drop down list.
There's a multitude of biomes to discover. Each with their own unique enemies, and of course, epic boss fights. There's an incredible number of things you can do as you progress through the game. And while it plays fine single player, if you have a friend or two you can bring with you on this journey, you'll have that much more fun and they will thank you for it.
Sure, you can spend hours upon hours building elaborate castles decorated with furniture you've crafted or statues you've collected from around the world. You can reshape the terrain around you - spreading biomes you like or cutting down those you don't. You can even bring biomes up from deep in the earth and set up the perfect potion mushroom farm right next to your base. One of my favorite things to do is to use the wiring system to set elaborate boobie traps around my fortifications. But you don't have to do any of that to progress. It's really all up to you. Although even if none of that is "your thing," you might be so drawn in that you find yourself happily engaged in such activities.
And yes, a big part of the game is digging, but it's primarily a means of exploration. A means of reaching that next treasure chest, or cluster of gems. A means of reaching the next deep fissure in the earth. A great adventure awaits you.

Satisfying builder and sandbox adventure with a sense of purpose and direction provided by increasingly difficult bosses.
What really sets this one apart is the in-depth mechanical system provided by the wiring and trap systems which can be used to creatively solve pretty much any problem the game throws at you. From beating the final boss in a few milliseconds to a teleporter hub that lets you easily access many parts of your world, your only real limit here is your patience.
If this doesn't appeal to you, the game can still be a fun romp with friends to go through and comes highly recommended to play multiplayer.

It took 6 long hours to beat this. This is my review on Sister Location:
This new FNAF took on a whole new mechanic, and it was great. Scott finally did something new with the series, and I can no longer call it repetitive. Every night, you get a whole new job to do, and it is brilliant because that means the game won't get stale and less scary during the players progression. Here's what I was expecting: You are in your room and you have to flash your lights and shock them and go through the vents incase of a power outage in one of their rooms. I thought it would be the 6 am job but with a sort of free roam. This is NOT what this game was. Let's go through the nights.
**SPOILERS AHEAD**
So as I remember, Night 1 was basically a tutorial of how everything worked in the rooms. Nothing special, really.
Night 2 is when things got scary. You would go to Babys area and have a power outage happen. You would hear someone telling you to hide under the desk because Baby is coming. For this night, you roll up a metal sheet with holes, and try to avoid Bidybabs eyeballs staring at you through them. This freaked me out, but luckily I got it in one try. You would then have to go to the Ballora gallery room and get past her by not creating much noise and stopping when you hear her tune. This was a pretty scary free roam type thing, and I thought it was awesome. Then you are in a room with Funtime Freddy. Basically put all the rooms online while playing a tape to get Freddy away from you. This was an awesome concept and reminded me of FNAF 3 in a way. Play it for yourself and you will see.
Night 3 is when things get scarier and scarier. Instead of going past Ballora, you'd have to go past Foxy, which is  much harder. What you do is stop and flash, and if she is in front of you keep flashing until she is gone from your sight. Stop and flash every 3-4 seconds. After getting past that, you will have to open up Funtime Freddy in this room. After doing all the procedures you have to click the button below the Bonnie puppets bowtie. To win this, you simply keep the light off of Bonnie and let it come out closer so you can click his button. Pretty difficult if you ask me.
Night 4 was the most stressful night of them all. The one that almost made me quit completely. You have to wind up the springlocks for a duration of 3 minutes while wiggling off Balloras minireenas on the sides of your mask. This took me 3 hours to do, and won by doing a zig zag pattern on the springlocks. After winning that, you're off with Baby. You have to do something similar to Funtime Freddy, but activate Baby to go top the scooper room. Either Baby or someone else guides you in the dark to the scoop room and all you have to do is listen to the voice. At one point, the voice tells you to stop and be silent, and means it, because it detects your microphone. After easily passing that, you get trapped in the scooper room by Ennard, whom I haven't seen in the game yet. The game ends there. This is what I experienced.
This game was scary, had some good humor, and a great story. I give it a solid 8.7/10.

I realize that this is a simulator, and that the scenarios that people create are about as real as the situations created in The Sims.  However, there's something surreal about the sims.  For me, Prison Architect is far too close to reality to be humorous or entertaining.  It's a good game, but I get deeply, deeply depressed, thinking about how somewhere out there, this exact, terrible scenario has probably happened, or could be happening right now.  It's disquieting at best, and gut wrenching at worst.  I know games desensitize us to a degree, but I just can't get desensitized enough to enjoy Prison Architect.  It might not look like it, but of all the games I own, it has the blackest, most horrifying basis.  Don't let the pixely seeming and the handful of interior jokes fool you.
I'm going to go back to something more cheerful, like zombie hoardes.

Well where do I start. What a brilliant game first of all. Like most, when I first saw the quirky graphics, I did not have high expectations. However, after a recommendation from a friend I gave it a go and was pleasantly surprised. The gameplay is excellent and the building is satisfying.
The tutorial is good, it does not hold your hand and does expect you to to figure some things out for yourself.
Building is a trial and error exercise and will often find yourself running out of money until you sell off your prison for more. There are hundreds, if not thousands of ways to go about the layout and how you structure your prison. They do not give you templates and you will often find yourself tweaking layouts here and there to forever improve the designs.
I really enjoyed the sandbox experience and the fact you can do whatever you like. There are tasks you can to achive such as reach a certain prison capacity or build your prisoners a library. These can be ignored and is entirely up to you how the prisoners live. (I find treating them well tends to works better but tyrant is just as fun).
The random events such as fights and gang wars give you something to consider. Do I take on lots of high risk prisoners and make more money or just stick with minimum security and deal with less fights.
I won't go on as I'm sure many other can explain it better the I, however I can not recommend this game enough.

When the game updates itself (and you can't do nothing about that), there's pretty high possibility that mods will not be compatible with that new version. BUT, if the game itself allows you to install mods, it should allow you to fix old savegames (profiles) so you don't lose everything you gained so far, just because new game version can't work with old mod and at the same time. So, when new version can't work with old mod, it's not the worst one - you  can't load old savegame at all, because game warns you that your savegame contains some data which depending on these very mods, so you're on your own. You can play it from scratch or to give up for good, as you have no option to postpone update or downgrade if something goes wrong.
I just can't understand why SCS is unable to offer savegame update or at least clound profile data with we can import in freshly created savegame, to continue where we stopped?
OK, I'm ready to lose my beloved mods, wider coverage and better equipment, but some of them are stock and should be working.
So, I'm sorry, but this is a big dealbreaker for me.

Writing a review about a game that is part of an established series is always hard. That's why whenever I consume any kind of media I like to evaluate them based on their own merits, as standalone experiences. But it's undoubtable that if you are a long time fan of the Hitman franchise there will be things here that you will love, and things that you will miss.
The first time you play a level you will be lost. You won't know the rules, you won't know the layout, guard positions, area restrictions and you will feel like a stumbling idiot. But the more you play the better you'll get. As a lot of people said already, this game is about repetition. But the good kind. Because you will get better and better, you'll take on harder and harder challenges and you will become a true hitman. BUT after a while it gets old. The game desperately needs a harder difficulty setting where enemy positions, weapon placements, tool placements, etc. are randomised too keep the game spiced up. Escalations and contracts help the matter somewhat as they tend to introduce new challenges. But after a certain number of replays there doesn't remain any reason to continue on a certain level simply because you've experienced everything and unlocked everything.
There are some intricate scenarios that will play out here, some are a bit absurd for some people's taste, but I feel like it's a perfect match for a Hitman game (they've always been a bit over the top). It has a morbid sense of humour that I apreciate very much, as a game about killing people should.
Now, the things that you might miss. There are some intricate details that are missing. Like how there's no carrying case for sniper rifles, no weapon costumisation, no double silverballers (although something tells me we might just see them later on), but overall I don't really miss any of these things. The game is great if you are willing to invest your time in it.
Best Hitman game by a far.

Lemon cakes - Time to make 3hrs
- 3 cups cake flour
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 6 eggs
- 2 cups white sugar
- 1 cup butter, softened
- 2 tsp grated lemon zest
- 2 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 cup plain yoghurt
1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease one 10 inch tube pan.
2. Sift the flour, baking soda, and salt together. Set mixture aside.
3. Separate the eggs. In a large bowl beat the egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add 1/2 cup of the sugar, beating until stiff glossy peaks form. Set aside.
4. Cream butter or margarine, 1 1/2 cups sugar, egg yolks, lemon zest, and lemon juice together until fluffy. Add flour mixture alternately with the yogurt to the egg yolk mixture. Gently fold in the egg whites and pour the batter into the prepared pan.
5. Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 50 to 60 minutes. Let cake cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to finish cooling. Serves 12.

I can easily say that this game is much more engaging than a typical FNAF game. Each night I did somthing different, and each task was memorable and challenging. Of course, the gameplay is still simple, usually only requiring the player to use one button and the mouse, but it's fun none the less.
One of my criticisms about the gameplay is that sometimes what I'm supposed to do is kind of vague, and sometimes the actions I perform with the mouse don't translate well with what I wanted to do in the game. What I mean by that is, if I have to urgently close a door using the mouse, I want to click and violently drag it closed, but in the game that hardly does anything to the door. In actuality, I had click and keep my mouse at the edge of the door, not to close it, but to keep it from opening all the way and then shut it when the animatronic gives up. There's lots of stuff like that throughout the game, but it's not that bad since you are given a checkpoint before each major task.
In my opinion, the most frustrating night was Night 4. There was a lack of feedback for what I was doing wrong, since you got the same jumpscare for the two possible ways you could die.

I really liked the characters. This game has a healthy dose of humor, in the form of a robot AI who "assists" you in your job similar to Wheatly from Portal 2.
The story is a lot more clear this time around. There's less "read this article on the wall","record and then listen to this audio backwards","decipher this weird Atari mini game" as there are in the other games (but they are still present here). The game has more dialouge, making it easier to follow, while you are playing.
The game ends a little unsatisfactory. My issue is you get kind of stuck in the end. You know when you watch a horror movie and your screaming at the protagonist to "DON'T SIT STILL, RUN!" That's how I felt. But I believe there is an alternate ending which is easy to access.
All in all, good game. I believe this is the strongest of the FNAF games.

Let's be clear here. I still haven't beaten the game, and part of the reason for that will be included in this. I have watched people finish the whole game.
So, let's get into this.
Sister Location is a weird departure from the main formula for a Five Nights at Freddy's game. It seems like it knows that the previous two games in the series(FNaF World and FNaF 4) did something wrong, and it really, really wants to try to fix that, but it kind of fails. It does a fantastic job of bringing in elements of the previous games. FNaF World's humor, the insane talent for listening you needed for FNaF 4, FNaF 3's audio, FNaF 2's music box, and the power mechanic from FNaF 1, although I can't tell you where for fear of spoilers.
The vampire soap opera inbetween nights is fantastic, from the voice acting to the animation. The story and the jumpscares feel like a typical FNaF game, but turned up to 11. There's an intense amount of focus that has to go into this game, if you want to even get past a night. You need different skills for each night, too, so I'd reccomend brushing up on the rest of your main series FNaF games.
The main thing about SL is that it feels like a spiritual recreation of the scrapped One Week at Flumpty's. It reeks of the game. Everything from the concept of only facing a couple enemies every night to the scrapped blind character in One Night at Flumpty's 2 shows up at some point in SL. I would be unsurprised if someone made a mod to make it as close as possible to OWaF. The other thing is the glitches. While they're minor, they're still annoying. There's a point early on in Night 2 where you should only be somewhere for a few minutes, then that section is done, but it often gets dragged out to ten minutes before you realize, "Hey, wait a second, nothing's happened for about five minutes. Shouldn't I be done?"
There's also Night 4. This is the worst part of the game. There are people that have already put hours of work into this night, and haven't beaten it. It doesn't work. It's incredibly difficult, to the point that you'll be sinking the kind of hours into it that you've put into the 20 modes in the other games. Practice the Golden Freddy Challenge in FNaF 2, if you're really looking to practice this part before buying the game. Night 4 is like doing that, but having ten music boxes to wind up while the animatronics in the center hallway don't actually do anything.
The secondary ending is also a pain. You have to go to extreme lengths to find it, and it's not even the real ending.
Overall, if you're looking for a good scare or incredibly confusing story, it's a good game. If you're looking for a true FNaF-styled game that goes by the formula, or for a generally good game, then you might want to avoid it. So, I do reccomend it, but only for die-hard fans of the series like myself.

I'm not going to go into depth here as you can find 10,000 other in depth reviews on the game through the power of the internet. I'll simply say it's a very balanced, well thought out game. The game has so many mechanics and systems working behind the scenes to bring to life a realistic portrayal of not only running the day to day of a prison but designing and then building it. Eventually expanding it, investing time and money into research to add that new Death Row cell block or say a nursery for those silly woman getting arrested while pregnant. You can create a namby pampy prison that uses soft, no tear bum hole paper and organic meals or crack down and punish even minor infractions with weeks or months in solitary. Give the prisoners essentially free roam of wide, open grounds or install shower heads in their cells and don't let them out even for yard or chow. OR you could be that slippery, greedy, narcissistic, egotistical CEO who gets a cut out of prisoners commisary, take bribes when catching inmates with shivs, favor building giant auditorium housing units or bunk bead cells over single prisoner cells. The options are endless. There is limitless replayability here on a Civilization V level. The game does a great job at presenting information you need in an admittedly mediocre user interface. The selection menus for objects and walls are a mess, never having a sort/filter option included and just in the order they were introduced in early access in. BUT I can't recall even once when I have found myself not able to answer a question I had. Or found out the root cause of an issue such as why all my prisoners are unhappy and fighting more often. Apparently prisoners don't like standing in a lunch line for 2 hours only to never get a tray of food, learn something new everyday I tell ya. A problem easily rectified by noticing you don't have enough cooks to cook enough meals in time and thus could hire more cooks, divide up the population and feed them at different times etc.
It might appear I lied when I said I wouldn't go in depth but honestly I haven't even covered half of the major systems Things visitation, parole board, death row, women prisoners with babies, utility piping/wiring, prisoner jobs, GANGS, religion, health, upgrading guards and their patrol patterns and loadouts all play roles in prisoner happiness, if they re-offend and come back to your prison etc. etc.
On another positive note the game was in early access for like 2 years. The developers were absolutely reliable and consistent for the entire time. Continous monthly updates like clock work. Substantial and feature filled updates. The game has a very active and well supported Steam Workshop support as well. Basically as long as the premise interests you and the strategy/simulation (it's a 50/50 mix) genre is your cup of tea there is a near non existent chance you'll be disappointed. It is worth $30 all damn day long. I'd say even $40 could be considered reasonable if strategy/simulation games were the genre you played most often.

as much, as often, and on as many computers you want forever and it's a simple .exe installer. Much more comforting than Steam's potential future situation. !!!!!!!!!!

Spec Ops may appear to be your average military shooter, but it uses that to its advantage to make you feel uncomfortable and question your actions.
